270	The cut covers the [In–Out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) when one is set, otherwise the whole length of the selected camera clips.
271	
272	Only the selected clips of a microphone's track are listened to. A camera track offers all its clips with a picture, selected or not, so an unselected clip on a camera track can still supply shots.
273	
274	## The summary
275	
276	The line under the controls says what **Switch** will do, for example "22 shots: 8 on Cam A, 14 on Cam B. Adds 23 clips." Cameras appear in the order they first show.
277	
278	When Switch can't go ahead, every reason replaces that line, one per line, and **Switch** stays dimmed. The sheet works this out again at every change, so change any control to check again.
279	
280	| The summary says | What it means |
281	| --- | --- |
282	| "The microphone on track … is still being analysed…" | Frame Job hasn't finished measuring that file's loudness or detecting its speech, which can happen straight after an import. Give it a moment, then change any control to check again. |
283	| "The microphone on track … has no speech between … and …, so it never says who is talking." | That microphone hears no speech in the range. Check you've paired the right track, or shorten the range. |
284	| "No angle has a picture between … and …." | No camera covers that stretch of the range. Set an In–Out range that avoids it, or fill the gap. |
285	| "The speaker on track … has no microphone." | A row has no microphone that's selected and sounding. |
286	| "The microphone on track … has no angle to show its speaker." | A row has no camera. |
287	| "Track … is the microphone for 2 speakers; each person needs their own microphone." | One microphone is on two rows. See [Good to know](#good-to-know) for when that's allowed. |
288	| "Switch by Speaker takes at most nine angles…" | More than nine tracks hold a selected picture. Select fewer. |
289	| "Switch by Speaker would add … clips to …; the most is 4096 — raise the minimum shot." | A project holds at most 4,096 clips. Raise [**Minimum shot**](/multicam/switch-settings/#minimum-shot) for fewer, longer shots. |
290	| "Speech detection is unavailable on this Mac, so Switch by Speaker cannot tell who is talking." | The on-device speech model can't run here, so the command can't work. |
291	| "The project's audio plan could not be read. Try again in a moment." | Frame Job couldn't read the project's sound just then. |
292	
293	An "angle" in these lines is a camera. The track number is Frame Job's own number for the track, not its position on the timeline. With one shared microphone, [two more lines](/multicam/one-microphone/#the-sheet-in-this-mode) can appear.
294	
295	**Switch** checks everything once more when you press it. If it can't go ahead at that moment, the reason shows in the summary and the sheet stays open.
296	
297	## How it chooses the shots
298	
299	- A cut lands a moment before each new speaker's first word. [**Cut**](/multicam/switch-settings/#cut-before-speech) sets how long.
300	- Silence holds the current shot, and so does a reply under a second long.
301	- A pause under half a second between one person's words doesn't end their turn.
302	- The cut opens on the [Wide](/multicam/switch-settings/#wide), the camera you've chosen for your wide shot, when there is one, otherwise on the first speaker's camera. With no Wide and nobody taking a turn, the range is one shot on the front-most camera.
303	- When two people talk at once, [**Crosstalk**](/multicam/switch-settings/#crosstalk-shows) decides what shows.
304	- Where a shot's camera has nothing to show, that stretch goes to the Wide, else the camera before it, else the front-most camera that covers it.
305	- A shot under [**Minimum shot**](/multicam/switch-settings/#minimum-shot) merges into a neighbour.
306	
307	## Linked cameras
308	
309	A camera clip still linked to its detached sound can't be switched. The sheet says so and names the clip, ending "Attach Audio first". Choose [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) to put the two back together, then try again.
310	
311	Only a linked camera clip crossing the range stops the cut.
312	
313	## One undo step
314	
315	**Switch** writes all of this as one undo step, **Switch by Speaker**. The selection stays. A selected clip cut at the range's ends brings its new half into the selection.
316	
317	### The Program track
318	
319	Switch adds a track named **Program** directly in front of the front-most camera. It holds a piece of the chosen camera for each shot, in sync, with the picture on and the sound off.
320	
321	To write over an earlier Program track instead, use [**Write to**](/multicam/switch-settings/#write-to).
322	----
323	---
324	title: "Cut from faces with one microphone"
325	description: When one microphone hears everyone, let Switch by Speaker decide who is talking from the cameras' pictures, and check the result.
326	---
327	
328	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
329	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
330	
331	When one microphone hears everyone, it can't say who's talking. [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) then decides from the cameras' pictures instead, by watching whose mouth is moving.
332	
333	<AtAGlance
334	  menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…"
335	  tools="switch_by_speaker"
336	  needs="Nothing. Face detection and speech detection run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
337	/>
338	
339	## One microphone for everyone
340	
341	Frame Job works this way when your selection holds exactly one microphone and two or more cameras. That includes a selection where only one camera has sound. See [Microphones](/multicam/set-up/#microphones).
342	
343	<Steps>
344	
345	1. Line the recordings up with **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**.
346	
347	2. Select the cameras' clips and the microphone's clip, then choose **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**.
348	
349	3. If the cameras haven't been read yet, wait for the [Analyzing sheet](#finding-faces-first).
350	
351	4. Check [the sheet](#the-sheet-in-this-mode) and choose **Switch**.
352	
353	5. [Look through the result](#faces-only-guess) and fix any wrong shots.
354	
355	</Steps>
356	
357	While the microphone hears speech, the camera whose person's mouth moves most is shown:
358	
359	- Each camera's person is the largest face in its picture.
360	- Frame Job watches that mouth opening and closing over half a second.
361	- A camera wins when its mouth moves at least half as much again as the next camera's (1.5×) and more than a small minimum.
362	- When two mouths move alike, or the busiest mouth stays under that minimum, it's crosstalk, and [**Crosstalk**](/multicam/switch-settings/#crosstalk-shows) decides what shows.
363	- With no speech, or no mouth to read, the current shot holds.
364	
365	The rest of the cut works as it does with several microphones, and it writes the same [Program track](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/#the-program-track) as one undo step.
366	
367	## Finding faces first
368	
369	Frame Job reads faces from its [on-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) of each camera. When a camera's faces haven't been found yet, an **Analyzing** sheet comes up first, with a bar for each file. The Switch by Speaker sheet opens once they're found.
370	
371	Only the part of each camera the range needs is analysed, and what's found is kept in the project's cache, so next time it's quicker or skipped.
372	
373	| If | Then |
374	| --- | --- |
375	| You choose **Stop** | Everything stays as it was, and what was saved so far is kept. Frame Job saves as it goes, every 30 seconds. Choose the command again to carry on. |
376	| The analysis fails | Frame Job beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector. |
377	| The project changed while it analysed | Frame Job beeps, says so at the foot of the inspector, and switches nothing. Choose the command again. |
378	
379	## The sheet in this mode
380	
381	The sheet changes to suit one microphone:
382	
383	- One **Microphone:** pop-up replaces the speaker rows, and **Cameras:** lists every camera.
384	- There's no **Ignore bleed** row, because there's no second microphone to bleed into.
385	- **Minimum shot** opens at 3 s, not 2 s, and isn't remembered.
386	- **Wide** opens on **None**.
387	
388	The other rows work as they do in [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/).
389	
390	A camera with no face whose mouth can be read stops the cut. The summary reads "The camera on track … shows no face whose mouth can be read between … and …, so it never says who is talking." A camera whose faces still aren't found reads "The camera on track … is still being analysed — its faces have not been found yet. Try again in a moment."
391	
392	## Wide in this mode
393	
394	Choose a **Wide** to show it during crosstalk. That camera then takes no part in deciding who talks, so a true wide shot whose faces are too small to read won't stop the cut. With no Wide, crosstalk holds the current shot.
395	
396	With only two cameras, making one the Wide leaves a single camera for faces to decide between. Faces no longer decide and the warning leaves the summary. The cut then opens on the Wide, moves to the other camera at the first turn of speech, and stays there unless [**Cut to the wide after**](/multicam/switch-settings/#cut-to-the-wide-after) breaks it up.
397	
398	## Faces only guess
399	
400	The summary starts "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts."
401	
402	Frame Job measures only how much each mouth moves while the microphone hears speech, so a mouth that moves without speaking, such as laughing or chewing, can put a cut in the wrong place. A face turned away gives no mouth to read, so that camera can't be chosen while it's turned, even if that person is the one talking. Look through the result and fix those shots with [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).
403	----
404	---
405	title: "Switch by Speaker settings"
406	description: What each row of the Switch by Speaker sheet does, its default and range, and which values Frame Job remembers.
407	---
408	
409	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
410	
411	These rows of the [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) sheet shape the cut: where it opens, how long shots last, and how it treats two people talking at once.
412	
413	<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…" tools="switch_by_speaker" />
414	
415	| Row | What it does | Default | Range |
416	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
417	| [**Wide:**](#wide) | Your wide shot, which opens the cut and shows during crosstalk | The one camera no person uses, otherwise None | Any camera, or None |
418	| [**Minimum shot:**](#minimum-shot) | The shortest shot allowed | 2 s (3 s with [one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)) | 0.5 to 30 s |
419	| [**Cut:**](#cut-before-speech) | How long before speech the cut comes | 0.2 s | 0 to 1 s |
420	| [**Crosstalk:**](#crosstalk-shows) | What shows while two people talk at once | Wide | Wide, Current speaker |
421	| [**Ignore bleed:**](#ignore-bleed) | How far below a speaker's level a voice is ignored | 15 dB | 3 to 40 dB |
422	| [**Cut to the wide after**](#cut-to-the-wide-after) | Breaks up a long monologue | Off | 2 to 600 s |
423	| [**Mute the cameras' own sound**](#mute-the-cameras-own-sound) | Turns the cameras' sound off inside the range | On when no microphone is on a camera track | |
424	| [**Write to:**](#write-to) | Where the cut goes | A new Program track | |
425	
426	The number fields take up to two decimal places.
427	
428	## Wide
429	
430	The camera for your wide shot. Choose any of the cameras, or **None**. If exactly one camera is left over once every person has theirs, it's picked to start with. Otherwise the row opens on **None**.
431	
432	The Wide shows:
433	
434	- at the start of the cut
435	- during crosstalk, when [**Crosstalk**](#crosstalk-shows) shows **Wide**
436	- after [**Cut to the wide after**](#cut-to-the-wide-after)
437	- for a stretch where another camera has nothing to show
438	
439	When nobody is talking, the current shot holds. It doesn't go to the Wide.
440	
441	## Minimum shot
442	
443	The shortest shot the cut may have, from 0.5 to 30 s. The default is 2 s.
444	
445	A shorter shot merges into the shot before it when that camera covers the stretch, otherwise into the shot after it. A short shot that neither neighbour covers stays.
446	
447	Raising this is also the way out when the cut would add more clips than a project can hold.
448	
449	## Cut before speech
450	
451	The **Cut:** row sets how long before a new speaker's first word the cut comes, from 0 to 1 s. The default is 0.2 s, and the cut lands on a whole frame.
452	
453	## Late cuts under heavy bleed
454	
455	A cut is timed from where a voice first rises above its [bleed](#ignore-bleed) line and the microphone's quiet background, not from the word itself. So with heavy bleed in a noisy room, a cut can land later than **Cut** asks. In the worst case measured, with another voice 24 dB down under −45 dBFS of noise, the cut came about 35 ms before the first word instead of 0.2 s.
456	
457	## Crosstalk shows
458	
459	What the program shows while two people talk at once for a second or more. **Wide** cuts to the [Wide](#wide), and **Current speaker** holds the shot you're on. With no Wide chosen, crosstalk holds the current shot whatever this says.
460	
461	Crosstalk shorter than a second starts nothing. A stretch under half a second between two bursts of crosstalk counts as crosstalk.
462	
463	Two microphones are crosstalk when both hear a voice above their [bleed](#ignore-bleed) line. If one leads the other by 8 dB or more, measured against each one's own speaker, it counts alone.
464	
465	## Ignore bleed
466	
467	Every microphone also hears the other people, quieter. A voice more than this far below a microphone's own speaker is bleed, and never counts as that person talking. It runs from 3 to 40 dB, and the default is 15 dB.
468	
469	- Raise it if a quiet guest is never shown.
470	- Lower it if someone is shown while only the other person talks.
471	
472	A voice must also stand 6 dB above the microphone's quiet background to count. This row doesn't appear in the [one-microphone sheet](/multicam/one-microphone/#the-sheet-in-this-mode).
473	
474	## Cut to the wide after
475	
476	Breaks up a long monologue. Tick the box and set how long one person may hold the screen, from 2 to 600 s. It's off by default, and the field offers 20 s.
477	
478	When a shot reaches that length, the Wide shows for one [**Minimum shot**](#minimum-shot), then the speaker's camera returns. This repeats to the end of the shot.
479	
480	It needs a Wide. With **Wide** on **None**, ticking it does nothing.
481	
482	## Mute the cameras' own sound
483	
484	Switches the cameras' scratch sound, the rough sound each camera recorded for itself, off inside the range. It's ticked to start with when no microphone is on a camera track, which is when the microphones are separate recordings.
485	
486	It never touches a microphone's track, so a camera used as a microphone keeps its sound.
487	
488	## Write to
489	
490	Writes the new cut over an earlier Program track instead of adding another. Choose **Replace the shots on** and the track's name, or leave it on **A new Program track**, the default.
491	
492	The row shows only when an earlier track can be replaced. That track must:
493	
494	- be unlocked
495	- hold no selected clip
496	- sit in front of the cameras
497	- have something in the range
498	- hold only pieces of the cameras there
499	
500	The track is cleared over the range and cut at its ends. Nothing on it outside the range changes.
501	
502	## Remembered values
503	
504	**Minimum shot**, **Cut**, **Crosstalk** and **Ignore bleed** are kept for the next time. They're written only when you change a value and press **Switch**, so **Cancel** keeps the old ones.
505	
506	**Minimum shot** isn't remembered in the one-microphone sheet. Every other row opens fresh each time. An agent's call reads none of the remembered values and uses the defaults in the table above.
507	
508	## With an agent
509	
510	`switch_by_speaker` takes these rows as `wide`, `min_shot`, `lead`, `crosstalk`, `bleed_db`, `wide_after`, `mute_cameras` and `track`. See [its options](/mcp/tools-multicam/#switch-by-speaker-options).
511	
512	## Related
513	
514	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
515	- [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)
516	- [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/)
517	- [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/)
518	
519	----
520	---
521	title: "Copy pieces to another track (agents)"
522	description: How an agent builds a program from synced cameras with copy_pieces, and what it can do with switch_by_speaker that the sheet can't.
523	---
524	
525	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
526	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
527	
528	An [agent](/mcp/overview/) can cut a multicam program more directly than the menus do. `copy_pieces` copies parts of a clip onto another track at the same times, and `switch_by_speaker` can preview a cut and use two values the sheet doesn't show. This page is for anyone driving Frame Job from an agent. The exact arguments and results of each tool are in [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).
529	
530	<AtAGlance
531	  where="No menu item of its own. Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ and Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker… write with it."
532	  tools={['copy_pieces', 'switch_by_speaker', 'switch_angle']}
533	  needs="Nothing. When there's only one microphone, faces are read on your Mac."
534	/>
535	
536	## Copy pieces of a clip
537	
538	`copy_pieces` takes the parts of one clip between the times you give and puts them on another track at the same times. It's what [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) are built from.
539	
540	| Argument | What it does | Required |
541	| --- | --- | --- |
542	| `clip` | The clip to copy from. | Yes |
543	| `track` | The track the pieces land on. It must be free over every range. | Yes |
544	| `ranges` | The stretches to copy, as `[[from, to], …]`, at least one pair. These are times on the timeline, in ticks, 600,000 a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). | Yes |
545	| `video` | Turns each piece's picture on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |
546	| `audio` | Turns each piece's sound on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |
547	
548	The whole call is one undo step, **Copy Pieces**. To work inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/), pass `scope`, and the times and tracks are then the nest's own.
549	
550	### What a piece is
551	
552	Each piece is exactly what splitting the clip at both ends of the range would leave in the middle. It shows the same source frames at the same times, so a piece of a synced camera stays in sync. It keeps the clip's speed, speed ramp, reversal and a graphic's own timeline, and its actions and timed words are cut the way a split cuts them.
553	
554	A piece gets a new id, has no transition, and isn't linked to any detached sound.
555	
556	### How ranges are read
557	
558	- Each range's ends snap to the frame grid.
559	- A pair written backwards is the same range.
560	- A range that's empty on the grid is skipped. If that leaves nothing, nothing changes.
561	- Ranges can touch, but they can't overlap.
562	
563	## Cut a whole program from the cameras
564	
565	An agent cuts a whole program with one `copy_pieces` per camera clip. The pieces land at the times they came from, so they fall into place around each other.
566	
567	<Steps>
568	
569	1. Add the program track with `add_track`, naming it. With no `index` it goes to the front, in front of the cameras.
570	
571	2. For each camera clip, call `copy_pieces` with that clip, the program track, and every stretch where the camera is on screen. This takes the stretches from 0 to 5 seconds and from 10 to 15 seconds:
572	
573	   ```json
574	   { "clip": 12, "track": 5, "ranges": [[0, 3000000], [6000000, 9000000]], "audio": false }
575	   ```
576	
577	3. If the sound comes from separate microphones, pass `audio: false` as above so the pieces stay silent, and mute the camera tracks with `set_track`, because they keep playing their own sound behind the program.
578	
579	</Steps>
580	
581	A range has to sit inside the one clip, so a camera that stopped and started needs a call for each of its clips.
582	
583	To change one shot afterwards, use `switch_angle`, the agent's form of [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/). See [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).
584	
585	## When a copy won't happen
586	
587	Nothing changes when one of these stops the copy. Frame Job checks them in this order and reports the first it meets:
588	
589	1. The clip is a nest. A piece of a nest would replay the nest from its first frame.
590	2. A range falls outside the clip.
591	3. Two ranges overlap.
592	4. The destination track is locked.
593	5. The destination track holds a clip over one of the ranges. The error names that clip and where it starts and ends. The clip you're copying from counts, so a piece can't land on its own track over itself.
594	
595	A copy that would take the project past 4,096 clips also fails.
596	
597	## Switch by Speaker from an agent
598	
599	`switch_by_speaker` cuts a Program track from the selected cameras, with the same values as the [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) sheet and the same result, as one undo step. [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) explains the values.
600

1	---
2	title: "Set up several cameras"
3	description: Put each camera on its own track, line them up by their sound, name them, and get a program track ready for a show filmed with more than one camera.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Set up a show filmed with several cameras, such as a podcast with a camera on each guest or an interview with a wide and a close shot, so you can cut between them.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio', 'Clip ▸ Split']}
13	  keys={['⌘T']}
14	  tools={['sync_audio', 'copy_pieces']}
15	/>
16	
17	## How multicam works
18	
19	There's no special multicam clip. Each camera is an ordinary clip on an ordinary track, and the edit you watch is a **program track** in front of them, made of pieces of whichever camera you want at each moment.
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Put [one camera on each track](#one-camera-per-track) and line them up.
24	2. [Name the tracks](#name-the-tracks) after their cameras.
25	3. Build [the program track](#the-program-track), by hand or with [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/).
26	4. Fix single shots with [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).
27	
28	</Steps>
29	
30	## One camera per track
31	
32	Put each camera's recording on a track of its own, then line the recordings up in time. **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** does this from their sound: select the recordings and choose it. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).
33	
34	If a camera stopped and started again, its pieces can all sit on the one track.
35	
36	## Name the tracks
37	
38	Double-click a track's header and type the camera's name. These names are what **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸** lists, and what the Switch by Speaker sheet uses for its cameras and microphones.
39	
40	When two listed tracks share a name, Frame Job adds each one's position counted from the back, for example "Camera (2)" and "Camera (3)".
41	
42	## The program track
43	
44	[Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) can write the whole program track for you, and it adds its own track.
45	
46	To build the program by hand:
47	
48	<Steps>
49	
50	1. Move the playhead to the start of a camera's clip.
51	2. Select the clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>, then <kbd>⌘V</kbd>. The copy lands at the playhead, in sync with the camera. A paste aims at the front track, and with a clip already there it makes a new track in front of the others. That track is your program.
52	3. With the copy selected, move the playhead to a cut and choose **Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>). Repeat for each cut, selecting the piece the cut falls in each time.
53	4. Select a shot and pick another camera from [**Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**](/multicam/switch-angle/).
54	
55	</Steps>
56	
57	The paste makes the track itself, so you don't need **Track ▸ New Track** (<kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd>) here. A track you added first is the front track, so the copy lands on it instead.
58	
59	A pasted copy keeps its sound on, so the same sound plays from the program track and the camera's track until you [mute one of them](/audio/mute-and-solo/). The pieces Switch by Speaker writes have their sound off.
60	
61	An agent builds the program with one `copy_pieces` call per camera. See [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/).
62	
63	## Shown or hidden
64	
65	The camera tracks stay underneath the program. Leave them shown and the program track, being in front, covers them. Or hide them with the hide switch in the track header, or **Hide Video** in the header's right-click menu. See [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
66	
67	Either way they still work as cameras: a hidden track's clips are still listed by Switch Angle and still count for Switch by Speaker.
68	
69	## Microphones
70	
71	Switch by Speaker needs to know which recording hears which person. It works this out from what you've selected.
72	
73	| Selected | What counts as a microphone |
74	| --- | --- |
75	| Clips with their sound on and no picture, such as a recorder or a separate microphone file | Every track holding one |
76	| No clips like that | Each camera that plays sound is its own microphone |
77	| A camera's sound split off with **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** | Never chosen for you, but you can pick it in a **Microphone** pop-up |
78	
79	So keep each person's microphone file on a track of its own, beside the cameras, and select it with them. Only the selected clips on a microphone's track are listened to.
80	
81	The sheet's **Microphone** pop-ups list every track holding a selected clip with its sound on, so you can swap in a detached camera sound or a camera's own sound there. An agent can name a detached camera sound as a microphone too.
82	
83	When the selection comes to exactly one microphone and two or more cameras, Switch by Speaker can't tell people apart by ear, so it decides from their faces. That includes the case where only one camera has sound. See [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/).
84	
85	## Related
86	
87	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
88	- [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)
89	- [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/)
90	- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
91	- [Add, rename and reorder tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/)
92	------
93	---
94	title: "Switch Angle"
95	description: Re-pick one shot of your program from another camera, in sync, over exactly the same span.
96	---
97	
98	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
99	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
100	
101	Switch Angle replaces one shot with another camera's picture over exactly the same span. Use it to fix a single cut after [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/), or to pick shots by hand. Your cameras need to be [lined up on tracks of their own](/multicam/set-up/) first.
102	
103	<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸" tools="switch_angle" />
104	
105	## Switch to another camera
106	
107	<Steps>
108	
109	1. Select the one shot you want to change, usually a clip on your [program track](/multicam/set-up/#the-program-track).
110	
111	2. Open **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**. The submenu [lists the cameras](#the-camera-list) that cover the whole shot.
112	
113	3. Choose a camera.
114	
115	</Steps>
116	
117	The whole switch is one undo step, called **Switch Angle**. The new clip is selected afterwards, or all of them if the shot became [several pieces](#a-camera-that-stopped-and-started). Switch Angle has no keyboard shortcut.
118	
119	## The camera list
120	
121	The submenu lists, front track first, every other track whose video clips cover the shot's whole span. Frame Job writes the list each time the menu opens, so it always matches the current selection.
122	
123	- Only clips of a video file with a picture count. Pictures, freeze frames, text, shapes, graphics and nests don't.
124	- A clip with its picture switched off still counts, and so does a clip on a hidden track. That's what keeps your cameras in the list after [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) has hidden them or turned their pictures off.
125	- The list stops at nine tracks. A tenth covering track, further back, isn't listed.
126	
127	### Tracks with the same name
128	
129	When two listed tracks share a name, each gets its position counted from the back track, for example **Camera (2)** and **Camera (3)**. A name only one listed track has appears as it is.
130	
131	### No Covering Angle
132	
133	The submenu holds a single greyed item, **No Covering Angle**, when there's nothing to switch to. That happens when you haven't selected exactly one clip, or when no track covers the selected clip. This item is never available.
134	
135	### Greyed cameras
136	
137	The cameras are listed but greyed when the switch can't be made:
138	
139	| Why it's greyed | What to do |
140	| --- | --- |
141	| The shot's track is locked. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
142	| The shot is linked to a detached sound. | Choose [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
143	| A sheet is open on the window. | Close the sheet. |
144	
145	## What the switch does
146	
147	The shot is replaced by the camera's picture on the shot's own track, over the same span and in sync. The new clip shows the camera's own frame at every moment, so a cut to it lands exactly where the old shot's cut did.
148	
149	### A camera that stopped and started
150	
151	A shot can cross the end of one of the camera's clips and the start of the next, when the camera stopped and started again. The shot then becomes two pieces, one from each file, meeting at a plain cut. A shot that crosses more of the camera's clips gets one piece for each.
152	
153	### Overlapping camera clips
154	
155	Where two of a camera's clips overlap, as they do across a transition, the later one takes over at its own start. The shot gets a piece of each, meeting at a plain cut, so a transition between those two clips doesn't appear in the shot.
156	
157	## What the shot keeps and loses
158	
159	The shot keeps:
160	
161	- Its span on the timeline.
162	- Whether its picture and its sound are on. A shot with its sound off gives you a new clip with its sound off, whatever the camera's clip has.
163	- The [transitions](/motion/transitions/) at both of its edges, with their kind, curve and audio shape.
164	
165	Nothing else carries over. A punch-in, a grade or an action on the old shot isn't copied to the new camera's piece. The piece is cut from the camera's own clip, so it has that clip's settings instead.
166	
167	## A transition that no longer fits
168	
169	A transition needs the two clips to overlap by its length. When the camera's first or last piece is too short for that, Frame Job drops that transition and makes the switch anyway, leaving a plain cut at that edge. The undo step then reads **Switch Angle (transition removed)**, so you can see that it happened.
170	
171	## When a switch fails
172	
173	When a switch can't be done, nothing changes. Frame Job beeps and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, after the word "Refused:". The message gives clips and tracks by number, and times in ticks, 600,000 to the second.
174	
175	| The message says | What it means |
176	| --- | --- |
177	| "clip 7's edge is held at tick …, short of tick …, so clip 9 cannot be re-picked" | The clip next to the shot plays a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) that can't give up the transition's frames. The message names that clip and the shot. |
178	| "track 3 does not cover clip 12: nothing with a picture plays on it at tick …" | The camera doesn't cover the shot, and the message names the first moment it doesn't. The menu only lists cameras that cover the shot, so this one normally comes back to an agent calling `switch_angle`. |
179	
180	## Good to know
181	
182	- Switch Angle works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), on the nest's own tracks.
183	- Only the shot's track has to be unlocked. A locked camera track is still listed, and you can switch to it.
184	- Frame Job doesn't check what kind of clip you've selected. A text or picture clip with a camera covering it gets replaced in the same way.
185	- A shot that becomes several pieces adds clips. At the project's limit of 4,096 clips, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes, with no message.
186	
187	## With an agent
188	
189	[`switch_angle`](/mcp/tools-multicam/#switch_angle) makes the same switch, and it takes the shot and the camera's track directly, so an agent isn't held to the menu's nine tracks. It returns the new clips rather than selecting them. To work inside a nest, open it with `set_scope` first, because the tool doesn't take `scope`.
190	
191	To lay a whole program out at once rather than one shot at a time, an agent can use [`copy_pieces`](/multicam/copy-pieces/).
192	
193	## Related
194	
195	- [Set up several cameras](/multicam/set-up/)
196	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
197	- [Transitions](/motion/transitions/)
198	- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
199	- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)
200	- [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/)
201	-----
202	---
203	title: "Switch by Speaker"
204	description: Cut a whole Program track from a conversation, showing whoever is talking on each microphone, as one undo step.
205	---
206	
207	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
208	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
209	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
210	
211	Switch by Speaker cuts a whole program for you from a conversation. It listens to each person's microphone and writes a new track that shows whoever is talking.
212	
213	<AtAGlance
214	  menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…"
215	  tools="switch_by_speaker"
216	  needs="Nothing. It reads each microphone's loudness and speech detection, made on your Mac at import, with no key and no upload."
217	/>
218	
219	## Cut a conversation
220	
221	<Steps>
222	
223	1. [Synchronize the recordings](#synchronize-first) with **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**.
224	
225	2. Select every camera's clips and every microphone's clips. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click each clip to add it, or <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag a band across them. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
226	
227	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it sits right after Synchronize Audio in the **Clip** menu.
228	
229	4. Check the [speaker rows](#speaker-rows) and adjust the [settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) if you need to. The [summary](#the-summary) at the foot of the sheet updates as you do.
230	
231	5. Choose **Switch** or press Return. **Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> leaves everything as it was.
232	
233	</Steps>
234	
235	<Shot
236	  name="15h-switch-by-speaker-sheet.sheet"
237	  alt="The Switch by Speaker sheet. Two speaker rows pair the Camera microphone with the Camera track and the Screen microphone with the Screen track. 241	
242	## Synchronize first
243	
244	Switch by Speaker trusts where the clips sit. It doesn't check that they're in sync, so run [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) before it.
245	
246	A camera [slipped](/editing/slip-and-roll/) or dragged afterwards puts its shots out of step with the voices.
247	
248	## When it is offered
249	
250	**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** is available when:
251	
252	- the selection holds clips with a picture on two or more tracks, each of which is a camera
253	- at least one selected clip has its sound on, from a file that has sound
254	- no sheet is open on the window
255	
256	Sound you've split off with **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** never makes its track a camera. The sheet handles up to nine cameras. The command is still offered with more, but the summary then says so and **Switch** stays dimmed.
257	
258	## Speaker rows
259	
260	Each person gets a row, reading **Speaker 1:**, then a microphone pop-up, the word "on", and the camera that shows them. A camera that is its own microphone stays paired with itself, and the rest are paired front to back to start with. See [Microphones](/multicam/set-up/#microphones) for how the microphones are chosen.
261	
262	Each person needs their own microphone and a camera. A pop-up offers **None** only where the selection left that row with nothing to pair. Leave it on **None** and the summary says what's missing.
263	
264	Change the rows when the front-to-back guess puts someone on the wrong camera. The microphones listed come from your selection, and the cameras from the tracks holding your selected pictures.
265	
266	With exactly one microphone and two or more cameras, the rows are replaced by a different layout. See [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/).
267	
268	## The range
269	
270	The cut covers the [In–Out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) when one is set, otherwise the whole length of the selected camera clips.
271	
272	Only the selected clips of a microphone's track are listened to. A camera track offers all its clips with a picture, selected or not, so an unselected clip on a camera track can still supply shots.
273	
274	## The summary
275	
276	The line under the controls says what **Switch** will do, for example "22 shots: 8 on Cam A, 14 on Cam B. Adds 23 clips." Cameras appear in the order they first show.
277	
278	When Switch can't go ahead, every reason replaces that line, one per line, and **Switch** stays dimmed. The sheet works this out again at every change, so change any control to check again.
279	
280	| The summary says | What it means |
281	| --- | --- |
282	| "The microphone on track … is still being analysed…" | Frame Job hasn't finished measuring that file's loudness or detecting its speech, which can happen straight after an import. Give it a moment, then change any control to check again. |
283	| "The microphone on track … has no speech between … and …, so it never says who is talking." | That microphone hears no speech in the range. Check you've paired the right track, or shorten the range. |
284	| "No angle has a picture between … and …." | No camera covers that stretch of the range. Set an In–Out range that avoids it, or fill the gap. |
285	| "The speaker on track … has no microphone." | A row has no microphone that's selected and sounding. |
286	| "The microphone on track … has no angle to show its speaker." | A row has no camera. |
287	| "Track … is the microphone for 2 speakers; each person needs their own microphone." | One microphone is on two rows. See [Good to know](#good-to-know) for when that's allowed. |
288	| "Switch by Speaker takes at most nine angles…" | More than nine tracks hold a selected picture. Select fewer. |
289	| "Switch by Speaker would add … clips to …; the most is 4096 — raise the minimum shot." | A project holds at most 4,096 clips. Raise [**Minimum shot**](/multicam/switch-settings/#minimum-shot) for fewer, longer shots. |
290	| "Speech detection is unavailable on this Mac, so Switch by Speaker cannot tell who is talking." | The on-device speech model can't run here, so the command can't work. |
291	| "The project's audio plan could not be read. Try again in a moment." | Frame Job couldn't read the project's sound just then. |
292	
293	An "angle" in these lines is a camera. The track number is Frame Job's own number for the track, not its position on the timeline. With one shared microphone, [two more lines](/multicam/one-microphone/#the-sheet-in-this-mode) can appear.
294	
295	**Switch** checks everything once more when you press it. If it can't go ahead at that moment, the reason shows in the summary and the sheet stays open.
296	
297	## How it chooses the shots
298	
299	- A cut lands a moment before each new speaker's first word. [**Cut**](/multicam/switch-settings/#cut-before-speech) sets how long.
300	- Silence holds the current shot, and so does a reply under a second long.
301	- A pause under half a second between one person's words doesn't end their turn.
302	- The cut opens on the [Wide](/multicam/switch-settings/#wide), the camera you've chosen for your wide shot, when there is one, otherwise on the first speaker's camera. With no Wide and nobody taking a turn, the range is one shot on the front-most camera.
303	- When two people talk at once, [**Crosstalk**](/multicam/switch-settings/#crosstalk-shows) decides what shows.
304	- Where a shot's camera has nothing to show, that stretch goes to the Wide, else the camera before it, else the front-most camera that covers it.
305	- A shot under [**Minimum shot**](/multicam/switch-settings/#minimum-shot) merges into a neighbour.
306	
307	## Linked cameras
308	
309	A camera clip still linked to its detached sound can't be switched. The sheet says so and names the clip, ending "Attach Audio first". Choose [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) to put the two back together, then try again.
310	
311	Only a linked camera clip crossing the range stops the cut.
312	
313	## One undo step
314	
315	**Switch** writes all of this as one undo step, **Switch by Speaker**. The selection stays. A selected clip cut at the range's ends brings its new half into the selection.
316	
317	### The Program track
318	
319	Switch adds a track named **Program** directly in front of the front-most camera. It holds a piece of the chosen camera for each shot, in sync, with the picture on and the sound off.
320	
321	To write over an earlier Program track instead, use [**Write to**](/multicam/switch-settings/#write-to).

339	## One microphone for everyone
340	
341	Frame Job works this way when your selection holds exactly one microphone and two or more cameras. That includes a selection where only one camera has sound. See [Microphones](/multicam/set-up/#microphones).
342	
343	<Steps>
344	
345	1. Line the recordings up with **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**.
346	
347	2. Select the cameras' clips and the microphone's clip, then choose **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**.
348	
349	3. If the cameras haven't been read yet, wait for the [Analyzing sheet](#finding-faces-first).
350	
351	4. Check [the sheet](#the-sheet-in-this-mode) and choose **Switch**.
352	
353	5. [Look through the result](#faces-only-guess) and fix any wrong shots.
354	
355	</Steps>
356	
357	While the microphone hears speech, the camera whose person's mouth moves most is shown:
358	
359	- Each camera's person is the largest face in its picture.
360	- Frame Job watches that mouth opening and closing over half a second.
361	- A camera wins when its mouth moves at least half as much again as the next camera's (1.5×) and more than a small minimum.
362	- When two mouths move alike, or the busiest mouth stays under that minimum, it's crosstalk, and [**Crosstalk**](/multicam/switch-settings/#crosstalk-shows) decides what shows.
363	- With no speech, or no mouth to read, the current shot holds.
364	
365	The rest of the cut works as it does with several microphones, and it writes the same [Program track](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/#the-program-track) as one undo step.
366	
367	## Finding faces first
368	
369	Frame Job reads faces from its [on-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) of each camera. When a camera's faces haven't been found yet, an **Analyzing** sheet comes up first, with a bar for each file. The Switch by Speaker sheet opens once they're found.
370	
371	Only the part of each camera the range needs is analysed, and what's found is kept in the project's cache, so next time it's quicker or skipped.
372	
373	| If | Then |
374	| --- | --- |
375	| You choose **Stop** | Everything stays as it was, and what was saved so far is kept. Frame Job saves as it goes, every 30 seconds. Choose the command again to carry on. |
376	| The analysis fails | Frame Job beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector. |
377	| The project changed while it analysed | Frame Job beeps, says so at the foot of the inspector, and switches nothing. Choose the command again. |
378	
379	## The sheet in this mode
380	
381	The sheet changes to suit one microphone:
382	
383	- One **Microphone:** pop-up replaces the speaker rows, and **Cameras:** lists every camera.
384	- There's no **Ignore bleed** row, because there's no second microphone to bleed into.
385	- **Minimum shot** opens at 3 s, not 2 s, and isn't remembered.
386	- **Wide** opens on **None**.
387	
388	The other rows work as they do in [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/).
389	
390	A camera with no face whose mouth can be read stops the cut. The summary reads "The camera on track … shows no face whose mouth can be read between … and …, so it never says who is talking." A camera whose faces still aren't found reads "The camera on track … is still being analysed — its faces have not been found yet. Try again in a moment."
391	
392	## Wide in this mode
393	
394	Choose a **Wide** to show it during crosstalk. That camera then takes no part in deciding who talks, so a true wide shot whose faces are too small to read won't stop the cut. With no Wide, crosstalk holds the current shot.
395	
396	With only two cameras, making one the Wide leaves a single camera for faces to decide between. Faces no longer decide and the warning leaves the summary. The cut then opens on the Wide, moves to the other camera at the first turn of speech, and stays there unless [**Cut to the wide after**](/multicam/switch-settings/#cut-to-the-wide-after) breaks it up.
397	
398	## Faces only guess
399	
400	The summary starts "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts."
401	
402	Frame Job measures only how much each mouth moves while the microphone hears speech, so a mouth that moves without speaking, such as laughing or chewing, can put a cut in the wrong place. A face turned away gives no mouth to read, so that camera can't be chosen while it's turned, even if that person is the one talking. Look through the result and fix those shots with [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).

411	These rows of the [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) sheet shape the cut: where it opens, how long shots last, and how it treats two people talking at once.
412	
413	<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…" tools="switch_by_speaker" />
414	
415	| Row | What it does | Default | Range |
416	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
417	| [**Wide:**](#wide) | Your wide shot, which opens the cut and shows during crosstalk | The one camera no person uses, otherwise None | Any camera, or None |
418	| [**Minimum shot:**](#minimum-shot) | The shortest shot allowed | 2 s (3 s with [one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)) | 0.5 to 30 s |
419	| [**Cut:**](#cut-before-speech) | How long before speech the cut comes | 0.2 s | 0 to 1 s |
420	| [**Crosstalk:**](#crosstalk-shows) | What shows while two people talk at once | Wide | Wide, Current speaker |
421	| [**Ignore bleed:**](#ignore-bleed) | How far below a speaker's level a voice is ignored | 15 dB | 3 to 40 dB |
422	| [**Cut to the wide after**](#cut-to-the-wide-after) | Breaks up a long monologue | Off | 2 to 600 s |
423	| [**Mute the cameras' own sound**](#mute-the-cameras-own-sound) | Turns the cameras' sound off inside the range | On when no microphone is on a camera track | |
424	| [**Write to:**](#write-to) | Where the cut goes | A new Program track | |
425	
426	The number fields take up to two decimal places.
427	
428	## Wide
429	
430	The camera for your wide shot. Choose any of the cameras, or **None**. If exactly one camera is left over once every person has theirs, it's picked to start with. Otherwise the row opens on **None**.
431	
432	The Wide shows:
433	
434	- at the start of the cut
435	- during crosstalk, when [**Crosstalk**](#crosstalk-shows) shows **Wide**
436	- after [**Cut to the wide after**](#cut-to-the-wide-after)
437	- for a stretch where another camera has nothing to show
438	
439	When nobody is talking, the current shot holds. It doesn't go to the Wide.
440	
441	## Minimum shot
442	
443	The shortest shot the cut may have, from 0.5 to 30 s. The default is 2 s.
444	
445	A shorter shot merges into the shot before it when that camera covers the stretch, otherwise into the shot after it. A short shot that neither neighbour covers stays.
446	
447	Raising this is also the way out when the cut would add more clips than a project can hold.
448	
449	## Cut before speech
450	
451	The **Cut:** row sets how long before a new speaker's first word the cut comes, from 0 to 1 s. The default is 0.2 s, and the cut lands on a whole frame.
452	
453	## Late cuts under heavy bleed
454	
455	A cut is timed from where a voice first rises above its [bleed](#ignore-bleed) line and the microphone's quiet background, not from the word itself. So with heavy bleed in a noisy room, a cut can land later than **Cut** asks. In the worst case measured, with another voice 24 dB down under −45 dBFS of noise, the cut came about 35 ms before the first word instead of 0.2 s.
456	
457	## Crosstalk shows
458	
459	What the program shows while two people talk at once for a second or more. **Wide** cuts to the [Wide](#wide), and **Current speaker** holds the shot you're on. With no Wide chosen, crosstalk holds the current shot whatever this says.
460	
461	Crosstalk shorter than a second starts nothing. A stretch under half a second between two bursts of crosstalk counts as crosstalk.
462	
463	Two microphones are crosstalk when both hear a voice above their [bleed](#ignore-bleed) line. If one leads the other by 8 dB or more, measured against each one's own speaker, it counts alone.
464	
465	## Ignore bleed
466	
467	Every microphone also hears the other people, quieter. A voice more than this far below a microphone's own speaker is bleed, and never counts as that person talking. It runs from 3 to 40 dB, and the default is 15 dB.
468	
469	- Raise it if a quiet guest is never shown.
470	- Lower it if someone is shown while only the other person talks.
471	
472	A voice must also stand 6 dB above the microphone's quiet background to count. This row doesn't appear in the [one-microphone sheet](/multicam/one-microphone/#the-sheet-in-this-mode).
473	
474	## Cut to the wide after
475	
476	Breaks up a long monologue. Tick the box and set how long one person may hold the screen, from 2 to 600 s. It's off by default, and the field offers 20 s.
477	
478	When a shot reaches that length, the Wide shows for one [**Minimum shot**](#minimum-shot), then the speaker's camera returns. This repeats to the end of the shot.
479	
480	It needs a Wide. With **Wide** on **None**, ticking it does nothing.
481	
482	## Mute the cameras' own sound
483	
484	Switches the cameras' scratch sound, the rough sound each camera recorded for itself, off inside the range. It's ticked to start with when no microphone is on a camera track, which is when the microphones are separate recordings.
485	
486	It never touches a microphone's track, so a camera used as a microphone keeps its sound.
487	
488	## Write to
489	
490	Writes the new cut over an earlier Program track instead of adding another. Choose **Replace the shots on** and the track's name, or leave it on **A new Program track**, the default.
491	
492	The row shows only when an earlier track can be replaced. That track must:
493	
494	- be unlocked
495	- hold no selected clip
496	- sit in front of the cameras
497	- have something in the range
498	- hold only pieces of the cameras there
499	
500	The track is cleared over the range and cut at its ends. Nothing on it outside the range changes.
501	
502	## Remembered values
503	
504	**Minimum shot**, **Cut**, **Crosstalk** and **Ignore bleed** are kept for the next time. They're written only when you change a value and press **Switch**, so **Cancel** keeps the old ones.
505	
506	**Minimum shot** isn't remembered in the one-microphone sheet. Every other row opens fresh each time. An agent's call reads none of the remembered values and uses the defaults in the table above.
507

509	
510	`switch_by_speaker` takes these rows as `wide`, `min_shot`, `lead`, `crosstalk`, `bleed_db`, `wide_after`, `mute_cameras` and `track`. See [its options](/mcp/tools-multicam/#switch-by-speaker-options).

528	An [agent](/mcp/overview/) can cut a multicam program more directly than the menus do. `copy_pieces` copies parts of a clip onto another track at the same times, and `switch_by_speaker` can preview a cut and use two values the sheet doesn't show. 536	## Copy pieces of a clip
537	
538	`copy_pieces` takes the parts of one clip between the times you give and puts them on another track at the same times. It's what [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) are built from.
539	
540	| Argument | What it does | Required |
541	| --- | --- | --- |
542	| `clip` | The clip to copy from. | Yes |
543	| `track` | The track the pieces land on. It must be free over every range. | Yes |
544	| `ranges` | The stretches to copy, as `[[from, to], …]`, at least one pair. These are times on the timeline, in ticks, 600,000 a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). | Yes |
545	| `video` | Turns each piece's picture on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |
546	| `audio` | Turns each piece's sound on or off. | No. Default: the clip's own setting. |
547	
548	The whole call is one undo step, **Copy Pieces**. To work inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/), pass `scope`, and the times and tracks are then the nest's own.
549	
550	### What a piece is
551	
552	Each piece is exactly what splitting the clip at both ends of the range would leave in the middle. It shows the same source frames at the same times, so a piece of a synced camera stays in sync. It keeps the clip's speed, speed ramp, reversal and a graphic's own timeline, and its actions and timed words are cut the way a split cuts them.
553	
554	A piece gets a new id, has no transition, and isn't linked to any detached sound.
555	
556	### How ranges are read
557	
558	- Each range's ends snap to the frame grid.
559	- A pair written backwards is the same range.
560	- A range that's empty on the grid is skipped. If that leaves nothing, nothing changes.
561	- Ranges can touch, but they can't overlap.
562	
563	## Cut a whole program from the cameras
564	
565	An agent cuts a whole program with one `copy_pieces` per camera clip. The pieces land at the times they came from, so they fall into place around each other.
566	
567	<Steps>
568	
569	1. Add the program track with `add_track`, naming it. With no `index` it goes to the front, in front of the cameras.
570	
571	2. For each camera clip, call `copy_pieces` with that clip, the program track, and every stretch where the camera is on screen. This takes the stretches from 0 to 5 seconds and from 10 to 15 seconds:
572	
573	   ```json
574	   { "clip": 12, "track": 5, "ranges": [[0, 3000000], [6000000, 9000000]], "audio": false }
575	   ```
576	
577	3. If the sound comes from separate microphones, pass `audio: false` as above so the pieces stay silent, and mute the camera tracks with `set_track`, because they keep playing their own sound behind the program.
578	
579	</Steps>
580	
581	A range has to sit inside the one clip, so a camera that stopped and started needs a call for each of its clips.
582	
583	To change one shot afterwards, use `switch_angle`, the agent's form of [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/). See [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).
584	
585	## When a copy won't happen
586	
587	Nothing changes when one of these stops the copy. Frame Job checks them in this order and reports the first it meets:
588	
589	1. The clip is a nest. A piece of a nest would replay the nest from its first frame.
590	2. A range falls outside the clip.
591	3. Two ranges overlap.
592	4. The destination track is locked.
593	5. The destination track holds a clip over one of the ranges. The error names that clip and where it starts and ends. The clip you're copying from counts, so a piece can't land on its own track over itself.
594	
595	A copy that would take the project past 4,096 clips also fails.
596	
597	## Switch by Speaker from an agent
598	
599	`switch_by_speaker` cuts a Program track from the selected cameras, with the same values as the [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) sheet and the same result, as one undo step. [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) explains the values.

---
title: Detach and Attach Audio
description: Split a clip's sound onto a linked clip of its own, keep the two in step, and merge them back into one clip.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Detach Audio splits a clip's sound onto its own clip, so you can trim, move or process the sound apart from the picture. Attach Audio merges the two back into one clip.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Mix"
  tools={['detach_audio', 'attach_audio', 'set_enabled']}
/>

## Detach audio

Select one or more clips and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>. **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** and the **Detach Audio** button in the [Mix section](/audio/pan-and-mono/) of the Sound sub-tab do the same. The menu item is greyed out until something is selected.

Each selected clip splits in two, as one undo step named "Detach Audio":

- The original clip keeps its picture, and its audio is switched off.
- A new clip appears on the track directly below. It plays only sound, from the same file, with the same in point, length and speed, and it keeps the original's audio settings and actions.

If the clip is already on the bottom track, Frame Job adds a new track underneath for the sound. Otherwise the sound always goes on the next track down, so make room there first, or drag the sound to another track afterwards.

The two clips are now a **linked pair**. Trim the sound on its own to make a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).

### When Detach Audio won't work

Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector:

| The reason says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "…media 2 has no audio track" | The clip's file has no sound. |
| "…its audio is switched off" | The clip has already been detached, or its sound is otherwise off. |
| "…it is not a media clip" | The clip is text, a shape, a graphic, a picture, a freeze frame, a nest or an adjustment clip. |
...

---
title: Nests
description: Collapse several clips into one clip that moves, trims, fades and transforms as a group, and open it back out when you're done.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing, and the clips inside stay as you built them.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Nest', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest']}
  keys={['⌘G', '⇧⌘G']}
  tools={['nest', 'unnest', 'set_clip']}
/>

## Make a nest

<Steps>

1. Select the clips.

2. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Nest**.

</Steps>

The clips are replaced by one nest clip, which is selected so you can move or transform it straight away. The nest is one undo step, called Nest.

The nest clip goes on the front-most track the selection used, and runs from the earliest start to the latest end, including any gaps. A matte track is the exception: the nest clip goes on the front-most track that isn't a matte, and a matte only stays one inside the nest if the track it cuts goes in with it. See [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/).

A clip's [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) goes in with it, unless the sound is on a locked track.

To work on the contents later, double-click the nest clip. See [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/).

## What a nest keeps

Inside the nest, clips keep their properties, [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) and transitions, their timing relative to each other and their stacking order. The earliest clip starts at 0 on the nest's own timeline.

The tracks inside are new, and each keeps the name, the hidden, muted, locked and solo states, and the volume and pan of the track it came from. There are two exceptions:

- The track the nest clip lands on still applies its volume and pan over the whole nest clip, so its copy inside starts at full volume and centred. A selection from one track sounds the same nested.
- A track [compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) isn't copied inside. The one on the nest clip's own track goes on working over the nest clip.

The nest clip itself starts at the default position and scale, at full opacity. It has a **Sound** tab only when something inside can make a sound.

## Name a nest

Nests are named `Nest 1`, `Nest 2` and so on. To give a nest clip your own name, select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> (**Clip ▸ Rename…**), or use the name field at the top of the Clip tab.

A double-click on a nest clip opens it, so it doesn't start a rename as it does on other clips.

title: "Core concepts"
description: "The ideas the rest of these docs lean on: projects, media and clips, tracks, the canvas, actions, nests and the frame grid."
---

A few ideas run through everything in Frame Job. This page says what each one is and links to where it's covered. For a quick definition of a single word, see the [Glossary](/reference/glossary/).

## Project

A project is one `.framejob` package: a single file in the Finder that holds the edit and its caches. The edit is the canvas, the media list, the tracks, the clips and the markers. Frame Job can rebuild the caches, but not the edit, and the edit is all a package needs in order to open. Each open project has its own window.

Your footage stays where it is, and the project remembers where to find it. If you want copies inside the package, ask for them with [Consolidate Media…](/projects/consolidate-media/). See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).

## Media and clips

**Media** is a file the project knows about. A **clip** is one placement of something on the timeline. A new clip from the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) covers the whole file, and you can place the same file as many times as you like.

| Clip kind | What it plays |
| --- | --- |
| video | A movie file's picture, with its sound if it has any |
| audio | A sound with no picture |
| still | One frozen frame of a movie |
| image | A picture file, such as a PNG, JPEG or HEIC |
| text | [Words you type](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/) |
| shape | [A drawn shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/) |
| graphic | [A motion graphic](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/) |
| nest | [A group of clips](#nests) standing as one |
| adjustment | [A grade](/color/adjustment-clips/) applied to everything behind it. It draws nothing of its own. |

Every clip that draws (video, image, still, text, shape, graphic and nest) is placed and edited the same way, with the same gestures and a **Picture** sub-tab. Crop and a few other Picture sections are only for movies, stills and pictures. Where a kind differs, its page says so.

## Tracks and stacking

There is one kind of track, and it holds any clip, so one track can mix kinds.

Tracks stack back to front. The top lane is the front-most and the bottom lane is the back, so a track higher in the timeline draws in front. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).

## The canvas

The canvas is the fixed frame every clip is drawn into, at the project's size and frame rate. You set its size, rate and background colour on the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).

A clip is placed on the canvas. Moving or scaling a clip never changes the canvas. See [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/).

## Actions

An action is a span of time on one clip over which its properties ease to an end state. When the span is over, the clip holds that state until a later action changes it.

An action's times are measured from the clip's own start, so it moves with the clip. Actions on one clip can't overlap, and a clip can have as many as fit end to end. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).

## Nests

A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. The group then moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing.

You can open a nest and edit inside it, and nests can contain nests, up to eight levels deep. A nest's canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).

## The frame grid

A clip's times always land on a whole frame of the project's frame rate, so you can't place a clip between two frames. Typed times, drags and agent calls all round to this grid of frames. A clip is always at least one frame long. See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/).

## Why clips never push each other

Dragging a clip never shoves its neighbours. Two clips on a track may overlap a little, and the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) sets how much. A drop the rule won't allow springs back to the last place that was allowed, and moves nothing else. A clip dropped to overlap the clip before it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap.

Other clips move only when a command says so, such as Ripple Delete, Close Gap, Insert, Freeze Frame and, for an agent, Insert Time. Locked tracks stay put through all of them.

## Related

- [Your first edit](/getting-started/first-edit/)
- [A tour of the editor window](/getting-started/editor-window/)
- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)
- [Glossary](/reference/glossary/)

title: New Project from Range
description: Keep one stretch of your timeline as a new project of its own, with its graphics and everything already measured, and leave the original as it is.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

New Project from Range opens a new project holding exactly the timeline's in/out range, moved to start at 0. Use it to lift a section out of a long edit to work on by itself. The project you made it from doesn't change. If you only want a file of that section, [export the range](/export/range/) instead.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ New Project from Range…" tools="new_project_from_range" />

## Make a project from a range

<Steps>

1. Set the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) with **Mark ▸ Set In** (<kbd>I</kbd>) and **Mark ▸ Set Out** (<kbd>O</kbd>).

2. Choose **File ▸ New Project from Range…**.

</Steps>

The new project opens in its own window straight away. There's no sheet to fill in, and the command has no key.

The item is dimmed when no range is set, while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, and while a sheet is on the window.

## What is kept

- **Clips across an edge** are cut there, the same way [Split](/editing/splitting/) cuts them. This happens on every track, locked or not, and a linked pair stays linked.
- **Clips wholly inside the range** are kept. Everything outside it goes.
- **A transition across an edge** becomes a hard start or end. The piece beyond the edge is dropped, and at the In edge the incoming piece starts with no transition.
- **Markers inside the range** are kept, on the same moments of the edit. A marker exactly on the Out frame isn't kept.
- **Tracks and the canvas** stay as they are, including any track that ends up empty and any lock.
- **Media no kept clip plays** is left out, unless a kept clip's look or a kept file's colour setting still uses it as a [LUT](/color/luts/), or a kept clip's **Hide While Silent** follows it. Nests no kept clip reaches are left out too.

## What comes with it

The new project brings what's already been measured, so nothing is measured again when it opens. For each media file it keeps:

- filmstrips, waveforms and loudness
- voice detection and sound-matching features
- transcripts read on this Mac
- [analyses](/projects/media-analysis/), such as shots, faces, people and salient regions, masks and sound events
- the backwards render of a [reversed clip](/speed/reverse/)

Media files themselves are never copied. The new project points at the same files as the original.

[Speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), [isolated voice](/audio/voice-isolation/) and [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) renders don't come along. They're made again when needed.

### Cloud transcripts

title: Follow the speaker in a vertical
description: Make a vertical version of a wide interview that cuts to whoever is talking, using a microphone per person.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A wide shot of two to four people doesn't fit a tall frame. Follow Speaker solves that: in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/), it reads each person's microphone and cuts the frame to whoever is talking.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
  where="Follow ▸ Speaker in the sheet"
  tools={['make_vertical_version', 'reframe_clip']}
  needs="A microphone for each person, on its own track. Faces are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## What you need

- A wide shot: a full-frame movie clip with the people in it.
- A sound file for each person, from a recorder or a lavalier rather than a camera, each on its own track and recorded with the shot.
- Those sound files lined up with the shot. Use [**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**](/audio/synchronize-audio/) first.

## Follow the speaker

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** and set **Follow** to **Speaker**. The **Microphones** and **Faces** rows appear.

2. Under [**Microphones**](#microphones), tick the tracks that belong to the people in the shot, two to four.

3. Under [**Faces**](#faces), check that each row names that microphone's person. If the movies haven't been analysed yet the pop-ups have no faces for now.

4. Choose **Make**. If an analysis has to run first, [the sheet comes back](#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis) when it's done, so you can do step 3 and choose **Make** there.

</Steps>

The other controls work as they do in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/#the-controls).

## Microphones

A checkbox for each track holding a sound file, named by the track and listed front to back. Sound from a movie file doesn't count, so a camera's track isn't offered, and neither is a track whose clips all have their sound off. The first four are ticked.

Tick the ones that belong to the people in the shot. **Make** needs two to four, so with more than four tracks listed, check which four are ticked.

When no full-frame movie plays beside two ticked microphones, the sheet says "No full-frame movie clip plays beside two of the ticked microphones, so nobody can be framed by who is talking." and **Make** stays dimmed. Check that the shot and the microphones overlap on the timeline.

## Faces

One row per ticked microphone, with a pop-up of the faces Frame Job found in the longest shot it can frame this way. Faces are numbered left to right, with where each sits across the picture: **Face 1 (42 % across)**.

Ticking or unticking a microphone rebuilds the rows and offers the match again for the new set. Otherwise your own choice stands.

### The automatic match

Frame Job matches each microphone to the face whose mouth moves while it talks. When the match is clear the pop-ups are already set, and the note under them reads "Each microphone is matched to the face that talks with it; change one if it is wrong." Check that each row names that microphone's person.

A match is clear when every microphone agrees with its face to at least 0.2, on a scale where 1 is perfect agreement and 0 is none. A face is counted when it's in at least a quarter of the shot, and four faces at most are considered.

### Choose a face

When the match isn't clear, each pop-up says **Choose a face** and the note reads "The faces do not show clearly who is on each microphone: choose each microphone's face." Pick each microphone's face yourself.

If the shot shows fewer faces than the ticked microphones under it, the pop-ups have no faces to offer. Untick the microphones of people who aren't in it.

## When Make is offered

**Make** is available when all of these are true:

- Two to four microphones are ticked.

title: "Cut by deleting words"
description: Select words in the Transcript tab and delete them, taking the picture and sound under them out of the timeline and closing the gap.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Editing a spoken video can work like editing text. Select words in the Transcript tab, press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, and the words and everything under them come out of the timeline, with the gap closed.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
  keys={['⌫', '⌦', '⌘⌫']}
  where="Inspector ▸ Transcript"
  tools={['get_timeline_transcript', 'get_transcript', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'set_range']}
  needs="Words in the Transcript tab, read on this Mac or from an AssemblyAI transcript. Cutting them uploads nothing."
/>

## Delete words

<Steps>

1. Choose **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>). The Transcript tab opens and its text takes the keyboard. The first time you look, the tab has to [read the file](/captions/transcript-words/), so the words can take a moment to appear.

2. [Select the words](#select-words) you want gone.

3. Look at what's shaded on the timeline. That's exactly what will go. To hear it first, turn on [Loop](/timeline/loop/), which plays the shaded range.

4. Press <kbd>⌫</kbd>.

</Steps>

The words and the sound under them come out of every unlocked track and the gap closes, as one undo step named **Delete Words**. The range clears and the playhead lands where the cut was.

<kbd>⌦</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, **Edit ▸ Delete** and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** all do the same thing here. On the timeline, <kbd>⌫</kbd> [leaves a gap](/editing/delete-clips/). In the transcript it closes the gap, the way deleting text does.

Deleting words one at a time gives the same result as deleting them together, unless a pause of more than a second lies between them. See [where a word cut falls](#where-a-word-cut-falls).

:::caution
These keys cut words only while the transcript text has the keyboard. If it doesn't, <kbd>⌫</kbd> does what it does on the timeline: with no clip selected, it lifts the shaded range and leaves a gap. Choose **View ▸ Transcript** first to give the text the keyboard. A click on a word would replace your selection.
:::

## Select words

| To | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Select one word | Click it. The playhead moves to it too. |
| Select a run of words | Drag across them. The text scrolls as you go, and a drag selects words only, never a pause. |
| Extend the selection | <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a word, or press <kbd>⇧</kbd> with an arrow. Neither moves the playhead. |
| Select every word | Press <kbd>⌘A</kbd>. |
---
| --- | --- |
| its audio is switched off | Turn the clip's audio on. |
| its media has no audio track | Nothing. The file has no sound to read. |
| its media file is missing | [Relink the file](/projects/relink-media/). |
| it plays in reverse, so its speech cannot be transcribed | Turn off [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) to read it. |

The first three clips are listed. "…and 4 more clips with no words." stands for the rest, and holding the pointer over it lists them.

## The same speech on two tracks

When two clips carry the same speech, such as a camera's sound and a separate microphone, a note names the pair:

> Clips 3 and 7 carry the same speech. Mute one, or switch its audio off, to read it once.

Both stay in the text until you do. The note appears for clips of different files that overlap for at least 5 seconds, when at least 60% of the words of the clip with fewer words in that overlap also appear in the other, in the same order.

## Good to know

- Nothing you do in the tab's bar changes the project, and the words aren't part of your edit.
- The tab has no search.

## With an agent

Agents read the same words with `get_timeline_transcript`. It returns the same notes as `notes` and the clips with no words as `no_words`, and its `tracks` and `language` do what **Words from** and **Language** do. See [`get_timeline_transcript`](/mcp/tools-captions/#get_timeline_transcript).

## Related

- [Where the transcript's words come from](/captions/transcript-words/)
- [Follow along and jump](/captions/follow-the-transcript/)
- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/)
- [Shorten a pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/)
- [Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/)
