title: Glossary
description: Frame Job's own words in plain terms, from action and canvas to nest, ramp, stem and tick, each linked to its page.
---

The words Frame Job uses, in plain terms, each with a link to the page that explains it.

## Projects and the timeline

- **Action.** An animation on a clip: a span on its action lane with an end state its properties ease to. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).
- **Adjustment clip.** A clip with no picture of its own that grades every track behind it. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
- **Canvas.** The fixed frame every clip is drawn into. Every export starts from its size. See [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/).
- **Clip.** One placed piece on a track: a stretch of a media file, or a text, shape, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
- **Current track.** The track of the first selected clip, or with nothing selected the front-most track. Track commands act on it. See [Menus](/reference/menus/).
- **Edit point.** A clip's start or end, where <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> stop. See [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
- **Frame grid.** The frames of the project's rate. Every time you set lands on one. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
- **In/out range.** The span set with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>, which many commands act on. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/).
- **Linked pair.** A picture clip and its detached sound, which move, split and ripple together. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
- **Media.** A file the project has imported, listed in the Media tab. Clips refer to it. See [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/).
- **Nest.** A clip that wraps other clips into a timeline of its own. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
- **No-change edit, or identity.** An edit that was understood and had nothing to change. It beeps, makes no undo step and shows no message. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/#a-beep-with-no-message).
- **Package.** A `.framejob` project, a folder the Finder shows as one file. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).
- **Playhead.** The current time on the timeline. See [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/).
- **Refusal.** A rule stopping an edit. Frame Job beeps and shows the rule's sentence after "Refused: " at the foot of the inspector. Nothing changes and no undo step is made. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
- **Ripple.** An edit that closes the gap it leaves by moving later clips along. See [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/).
- **Selected action.** The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing. While it's chosen, the fields show and write its end state. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/).
- **Tick.** Frame Job's unit of time, 600,000 to the second, which divides every common frame duration exactly. The "Refused: " line and agent tools give lengths in ticks. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
- **Track.** A lane of clips. The front track is the top lane, and it's drawn over those behind it. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).

## Picture and sound

- **Camera Log.** A file's setting saying which camera log curve it holds, so it's converted at the start of the picture. See [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
- **Cue.** One timed caption. See [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/).
- **Cutout.** A clip with Remove Background on. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).
- **Deep.** A picture with more than 8 bits for each colour component. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).
- **Ducking.** Lowering a clip's sound under another's. See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/).
- **Dynamic range.** Whether the project works in SDR or HDR (HLG). See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).
- **J-cut and L-cut.** The sound of a linked pair starting before, or ending after, its picture. See [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
- **Look.** A built-in grade or a `.cube` LUT on a clip. See [Looks](/color/looks/).
- **LUFS.** The unit of loudness. See [Normalize](/audio/normalize/).

20:- **Nest.** A clip that wraps other clips into a timeline of its own. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
23:- **Playhead.** The current time on the timeline. See [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/).
28:- **Track.** A lane of clips. The front track is the top lane, and it's drawn over those behind it. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).
42:- **Matte.** A track that cuts the track behind it by its alpha or brightness. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/).
48:- **Stem.** One track's sound written as its own file beside the mix. See [Audio stems](/export/stems/).
49:- **Transition.** The change from one clip to the next across their overlap on one track. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).

36	| "…media 2 has no audio track" | The clip's file has no sound. |
37	| "…its audio is switched off" | The clip has already been detached, or its sound is otherwise off. |
38	| "…it is not a media clip" | The clip is text, a shape, a graphic, a picture, a freeze frame, a nest or an adjustment clip. |
39	| "clips 4 and 7 would overlap by…, more than half of the shorter clip…" | The track below already has a clip where the sound would land. |
40	| "clip 4 would overlap more than one neighbour on one side…" | The sound would reach more than one clip on the track below. |
41	| "clips 4 and 7 would overlap, and clip 7 is an adjustment clip…" | The track below has an adjustment clip where the sound would land. |
42	
43	Any other overlap with one clip on the track below, up to half the shorter clip, is allowed and becomes a cross dissolve between the two.
44	
45	With several clips selected, the ones that can be detached are, and the rest are skipped. You only see a reason when none of them could be.
46	
47	## See which clips are linked
48	
49	Each half of a linked pair shows a link symbol after its kind symbol, in the clip's name strip. Select one and the other gets a dashed ring in your Mac's accent colour, because edits to one move both. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/#linked-clips).
50	
51	### A clip with its audio off
52	
53	A clip whose audio is off shows no waveform and no fade handles. A clip with its picture and its sound both off is drawn dimmed. The picture half of a linked pair has no Sound sub-tab, so select the sound half to change anything about the sound. See [Turn a clip's picture or sound off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).
54	
55	## What stays in sync
56	
57	A linked picture and sound stay in step in time through your edits.
58	
59	| Edit | What happens to the pair |
60	| --- | --- |

63	title: "Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift"
64	description: "Remove clips or a stretch of the timeline, and choose whether the hole stays open or closes up."
65	---
66	
67	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
68	
69	There are two delete keys, and the difference between them is what happens to the hole. <kbd>⌫</kbd> leaves it open, so everything else keeps its timing. <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> closes it, so the rest of the timeline moves left.
70	
71	<AtAGlance
72	  menu={['Edit ▸ Delete', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete']}
73	  keys={['⌫', '⌘⌫']}
74	  where="The Ripple Delete button in the timeline bar"
75	  tools={['delete', 'ripple_delete', 'lift_range', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
76	/>
77	
78	## Choose a delete
79	
80	Each key acts on the selection, or on the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) when nothing is selected.
81	
82	| | Clips selected | Nothing selected, a range set |
83	| --- | --- | --- |
84	| <kbd>⌫</kbd> **Edit ▸ Delete** | **Delete:** removes the clips and leaves gaps. | **Lift:** removes what's in the range and moves nothing. |
85	| <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** | **Ripple Delete:** removes the clips and closes each hole. | **Ripple Delete:** removes what's in the range and closes the hole. |
86	
87	A selection takes priority over a range, so [deselect](/timeline/selecting-clips/) first to act on the range. An empty range is ignored. With nothing to remove, both menu items are greyed out and the keys beep.
88	
89	## Delete clips and leave a gap
90	
91	Select the clips and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. They go, the gaps stay, and nothing else moves. It's one undo step, named Delete.
92	
93	- A picture takes its [linked sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) with it, unless the sound's track is locked.
94	- A linked sound clip goes alone, and leaves its picture silent.
95	- A clip on a locked track that you selected by clicking is still removed.
96	
97	## Ripple delete clips
98	
99	Select the clips and press <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, or use the timeline bar's button. The clips go, and each hole closes: everything later on every unlocked track moves left. It's one undo step, named Ripple Delete.
100	
101	- Each clip's linked partner on an unlocked track goes too, whichever half you selected.
102	- A clip on a locked track that you selected is removed, but clips on locked tracks don't move.
103	- [Markers](/timeline/markers/) don't move.
104	
105	:::caution
106	Unlike <kbd>⌫</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> ignores a [selected action](/motion/select-an-action/). With an action selected it ripple-deletes the whole clip. Undo brings it back.
107	:::
108	
109	## Lift a range
110	
111	Set an in/out range, select nothing and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, and what lies between is removed. Nothing moves, markers included. It's one undo step, named Lift.
112	
113	Lift is the safe cut when a mix or a caption track is already timed, because everything after the range keeps its moment. Clips on locked tracks are neither cut nor removed. If the range held nothing to remove, Frame Job beeps.
114	
115	## Ripple delete a range
116	
117	Set an in/out range, select nothing and press <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, what lies between is removed, and the hole closes. It's one undo step, named Ripple Delete.
118	
119	Clips on locked tracks are neither cut, removed nor moved, even inside the range. Everything else after the range moves left by its length, so a locked track falls out of step with the rest. That's what the lock is for.
120	
121	## How a ripple closes holes
122	
123	Each hole closes with one shift of everything after it, so clips that touched before still touch.
124	
125	- A clip past several holes moves by their combined length. Two removed clips that touch leave one hole.
126	- A clip moves if it starts at or after the end of the hole. When you ripple-delete clips, a clip on another track that spans the hole stays where it is, and isn't shortened.
127	- A clip's linked partner on an unlocked track moves with it.
128	- Markers stay at their times, because a marker inside a removed stretch would have nowhere to go.
129	- A clip that slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. A ripple is never stopped by the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
130	
131	One thing does stop a ripple. If it would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline, as a sound leading its picture in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) can, nothing moves, and the foot of the inspector names both clips.
132	
133	## Ripple delete several ranges
134	
135	An agent can cut a list of time ranges out of the timeline as one edit and one undo step, with [`ripple_delete_ranges`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_ranges). It shows as Ripple Delete under **Edit ▸ Undo**. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) make the same cut from their sheets.
136	
137	Ranges that touch or overlap merge into one before anything is cut, so two ranges that meet leave one hole, and all the cuts use times from the timeline as it was before the edit. Each range then behaves as [a ripple-deleted range](#ripple-delete-a-range) does: locked tracks are left alone and markers don't move. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).
138	
139	## When the delete keys do something else
140	
141	<kbd>⌫</kbd> removes the first of these it finds:
142	
143	1. Words or a pause selected in the [Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/), while that tab has the focus. They ripple out and the gap closes, as deleting text does.
144	2. A [selected action](/motion/change-an-action/). The action goes and its clip stays.
145	3. The selected clips.
146	4. The in/out range.
147	
148	<kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> follows the same order without the second step.
149	
150	While you type in a text field, both menu items are greyed out, so <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> edit the text. That covers the timecode fields, a rename and a text clip.
151

153	---
154	title: "How a clean-up cut works"
155	description: "What Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words share: the preview, the single undo step, how far a cut reaches, and what it won't touch."
156	---
157	
158	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
159	
160	Frame Job's two clean-up commands cut the same way. Each shows you what it would take out, makes the whole cut as one edit, closes the timeline over it, and stays out of nests and transitions. This page covers what they share.
161	
162	<AtAGlance
163	  menu={['Clip ▸ Remove Silences…', 'Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…']}
164	  tools={['detect_silence', 'detect_fillers', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
165	/>
166	
167	## Two commands for a spoken recording
168	
169	Both commands are for a screencast, a tutorial or a talking-head take.
170	
171	- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) cuts the dead air.
172	- [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) cuts the ums and uhs, using the timing of each word in a transcript.
173	
174	They're in the **Clip** menu, below **Close Gap** and **Retime Range…**, with **Remove Silences…** first. Neither has a keyboard shortcut.
175	
176	Remove Silences measures the mix as you hear it, so [volume](/audio/volume/), [fades](/audio/fades/), [ducking](/audio/ducking/), [mute and solo](/audio/mute-and-solo/) all change what it finds. See [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/).
177	
178	An agent can use both, and can also read a clip's transcript to [cut false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/).
179	
180	## See the cut before you make it
181	
182	Nothing changes until you choose **Remove**. While a sheet is open, it and the timeline show you exactly what would go.
183	
184	### Preview shading on the timeline
185	
186	Every span the command would remove is shaded on the timeline ruler and lanes.
187	
188	The shading is coral, about twice as strong as the wash of the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), so you can tell the two apart where they overlap. In the lanes it sits under the clips. On the ruler it sits under the ticks and marker flags, which stay readable.
189	
190	The shading goes away when the sheet closes, however it closes: **Remove**, **Cancel**, <kbd>⎋</kbd> or the window closing.
191	
192	### The cut count
193	
194	The sheet reads how many cuts it would make and how much time they remove, for example "23 cuts · removes 00:00:04:12". A single cut reads "1 cut". With nothing to cut it reads "No cuts", and **Remove** is dimmed.
195	
196	**Remove** makes exactly the cuts the count describes.
197	
198	### The rest of the editor waits
199	
200	Playback pauses when a sheet opens, because a moving playhead would repaint over the shading. Other editing commands in that window are off until you close the sheet.
201	
202	## One undo step
203	
204	**Remove** cuts every span and closes the timeline over each one as a single undo step, however many spans there are. One <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> restores everything. The step is named **Undo Remove Silences** or **Undo Remove Filler Words**.
205	
206	Spans that touch or overlap become one cut.
207	
208	[Deleting selected words](/captions/delete-words/) in the Transcript tab with <kbd>⌫</kbd> makes the same kind of cut, as its own step named Delete Words.
209	
210	## A ripple across every unlocked track
211	
212	A clean-up cut is a [ripple delete](/editing/delete-clips/#how-a-ripple-closes-holes) across every unlocked track, not only the clips that were analysed. The picture above a voice-over is cut with it, so the two stay in step.
213	
214	- **Working on selected clips doesn't limit the cut.** It changes what's listened to or read. The cut still reaches every unlocked track.
215	- **Locked tracks are neither cut nor moved.** Everything else closes up, so a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) falls out of step with the rest.
216	- **Linked clips move together.** If a clip that moves has a linked partner, the partner moves too. When that would take a clip before the start of the timeline, Frame Job makes no cut at all. It beeps, and the foot of the inspector names both clips.
217	
218	### Markers keep their place
219	
220	[Markers](/timeline/markers/) stay at their times when the timeline closes, as they do under every ripple delete. The footnote of both sheets says so: "markers keep their place". A marker after a cut therefore sits over later material than it did, so check any you placed on a particular moment.
221	
222	## Frame-accurate edges
223	
224	Each cut's start rounds up to the next frame and its end rounds down. Both edges move inward, so each edge of a cut can leave up to a frame of room tone, or of a filler, behind. Rounding outward would clip the start of the next word, so a cut never does.
225	
226	## Nests are protected
227	
228	A clean-up cut never reaches into a nest clip. A [nest](/editing/nests/) always plays from its first frame, so cutting into one would strand the rest of it. The whole nest can still slide left with everything else when the timeline closes up.
229	
230	In Remove Silences a nest's sound still counts when **In:** is **All audible clips**. A loud nest keeps a moment from being quiet, even though no cut may touch the nest.
231	
232	To clean up the audio inside a nest, do one of these:

235	title: Audio-only exports
236	description: Export the timeline's sound with no picture, as a compressed M4A or an uncompressed WAV or AIFF.
237	---
238	
239	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
240	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
241	
242	Frame Job can write the timeline's sound with no picture: an M4A to send to someone, or a WAV or AIFF to hand to a mastering engineer, a DAW or a podcast editor.
243	
244	<AtAGlance
245	  menu="File ▸ Export…"
246	  keys="⌘E"
247	  where="Export sheet ▸ Format"
248	  tools="export"
249	/>
250	
251	## Export the sound
252	
253	<Steps>
254	
255	1. Choose **File ▸ Export…** or press <kbd>⌘E</kbd>.
256	
257	2. In **Format**, choose **Audio only (M4A)**, **Audio only (WAV)** or **Audio only (AIFF)**.
258	
259	3. Set the [controls that apply](#which-controls-apply). The [readout](/export/export-sheet/#the-readout-line) under the controls shows the length in milliseconds rather than frames, for example `Audio only · 00:01:12.200`.
260	
261	4. Choose **Export…**, or **Add to Queue** to keep editing while it's written, then name the file.
262	
263	</Steps>
264	
265	## Audio only (M4A)
266	
267	An `.m4a` file holding AAC sound, 48 kHz stereo. This is the one to send to someone, because it's by far the smallest.
268	
269	The sound is 192 kbps unless you pick a tier in [Quality](/export/quality/): **Low** is 128 kbps, **Medium** 192, **High** 256 and **Maximum** 320. The footnote reads `AAC · M4A`, with the rate added when you pick a tier.
270	
271	Chapter markers are written into the file as [chapters](/export/chapters/), and the file is written with fast start, so a player can begin before all of it has arrived.
272	
273	## Audio only (WAV)
274	
275	A `.wav` file of uncompressed sound, 48 kHz stereo. Choose it when the mix is going into someone else's tool, where a second round of lossy compression is the one thing you can't take back.
276	
277	It's 16-bit by default, or 24-bit through [Bit depth](/export/bit-depth/). That's about 11.5 MB a minute at 16 bits and 17.3 MB a minute at 24. The footnote reads `LPCM · WAV`, with `24-bit` added at that depth.
278	
279	A WAV holds no chapters, so chapter markers are left out.
280	
281	## Audio only (AIFF)
282	
283	The same samples as a WAV, in an `.aiff` file. WAV stores each sample little-endian and AIFF big-endian, which matters only to the software reading the file, so choose whichever your tool asks for.
284	
285	Everything else is as for WAV: 48 kHz stereo, 16 or 24 bits, the same file size and no chapters. The footnote reads `LPCM · AIFF`.
286	
287	## Which controls apply
288	
289	A control an audio format can't use is greyed out. It keeps what it shows, and nothing from it reaches the file.
290	
291	| Control | M4A | WAV and AIFF |
292	| --- | --- | --- |
293	| **Quality** | Sets the AAC rate | Greyed out |
294	| **Bit depth** | Greyed out | 16-bit or 24-bit |
295	| [**Stems**](/export/stems/) | Available | Available |
296	| [**Loudness**](/export/loudness/) | Available | Available |
297	| [**Range**](/export/range/) | Available | Available |
298	| **Size**, **Frame rate**, **Speed**, **Burn in timecode** | Greyed out | Greyed out |
299	
300	**Size** has nothing to set because there's no picture. A preset saved from an audio format stores no size, so it can't carry one over to a movie.
301	
302	## The 48 kHz stereo master
303	
304	Every export with sound, movies included, reads the mix once as 48 kHz stereo at 32-bit float, and rounds it once at the very end. In between, the loudness gain and the limiter both work on the float mix, so nothing has been clipped before they act.
305	
306	The limiter holds the file's true peak at or under −1 dBTP. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/). Sound under that ceiling passes through unchanged.
307	
308	The final rounding goes to the nearest value at the file's bit depth, with no dither at 16 or 24 bits.
309	
310	There's no control for the sample rate or the channel count. Whatever your sources are, the file is 48 kHz stereo.
311	
312	## Good to know
313	
314	- A timeline with no sound at all can't be exported as audio. The export stops with "There is nothing on the timeline to export — add a clip first."
315	- [Stems](/export/stems/) skip the master's limiter, so a stem can peak higher than the mix.
316	- When the export finishes, the sheet reports what the sound measured. See [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/).
317	
318	## With an agent
319	
320	An agent passes `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` or `audio_aiff` as the `preset` of `export`. It sets the M4A's rate with `audio_bitrate` and a WAV or AIFF's depth with `audio_bits`. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
321

331	title: "Project frame rate"
332	description: "Choose the rate your project runs at, match it to your footage, and see what a rate change does to the timeline."
333	---
334	
335	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
336	
337	The project's frame rate sets the grid that every edit lands on. A new project runs at 30 fps, and a project opened from a movie takes the movie's rate. A rate chosen for one export is separate: see [Export frame rate](/export/frame-rate/).
338	
339	<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Frame Rate" tools="set_canvas" />
340	
341	## Choose a rate
342	
343	In the **Frame Rate** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/), choose a rate from **Rate**: **24**, **23.976**, **25**, **30**, **29.97**, **50**, **60** or **Match First Clip**.
344	
345	The change is one undo step. See [what it does to the timeline](#what-a-rate-change-does).
346	
347	## Match the first clip
348	
349	**Match First Clip** takes the rate of the earliest clip on the timeline whose file has video. It beeps if there isn't one.
350	
351	It sets the rate once, and later changes to the timeline don't move it. The popup then shows that rate, if it [lists it](#rates-the-popup-doesnt-list). A picture counts as having video here, and it reads as 30 fps.
352	
353	## Rates the popup doesn't list
354	
355	A project can run at a rate the popup doesn't have, because a file's rate is kept as it is when you open it.
356	
357	- A file at 24, 23.976, 25, 30, 29.97, 48, 50, 60 or 59.94 fps keeps that exact rate.
358	- Any other rate is kept to three decimals, so a 47.3 fps recording stays at 47.3 and doesn't become 48. Screen recordings often have odd rates.
359	
360	:::caution
361	At a rate it doesn't list, **Rate** shows **24**. The **Frame rate** row at the top of the Document tab shows the real rate, so trust that one.
362	:::
363	
364	Choosing a popup item changes the rate. **Match First Clip** brings the file's own rate back.
365	
366	## What a rate change does
367	
368	Changing the rate moves every clip start, clip length, action and marker onto the new frame grid, inside nests as well.
369	
370	- A clip's length is held to the media it has left, so a coarser grid can't push a clip past the end of its file.
371	- A clip always keeps at least one frame.
372	- An action stays inside its clip. A speed ramp's action is only snapped to the new grid.
373	- Where a clip starts reading its source doesn't change, and sound fades keep their lengths.
374	
375	If two markers land on the same frame at the new rate, only one stays: the one added first.
376	
377	Frame Job doesn't check the new positions for overlaps, and it won't stop a rate change because of one. Each edge moves by less than a frame, so an overlap can grow by a frame at most.
378	
379	## Read the timeline's length
380	
381	**Duration**, under **Rate**, is a read-only row showing the timeline's length in the project's [timecode format](/projects/background-and-timecode/#choose-a-timecode-format).
382	
383	## With an agent
384	
385	[`set_canvas`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_canvas) takes `fps` as `[numerator, denominator]`: `[30, 1]`, `[30000, 1001]` for 29.97 or `[24000, 1001]` for 23.976. Any fraction works, so an agent can set a rate the popup doesn't list, such as 48 or 59.94 fps. A 0 in either place fails and the rate stays as it was. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
386

394	title: Troubleshooting
395	description: Find out why a command is greyed, an edit is refused, a file won't open, a clip is silent or an export stops, and what to do next.
396	---
397	
398	Frame Job says why it won't do something, in a sentence or a tooltip. This page starts from what you see and tells you what it means and what to do. For the numbers behind these answers, see [Limits](/reference/limits/).
399	
400	## A command is greyed out
401	
402	Every menu item has a rule for when it's on. [Menus](/reference/menus/) and [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/) give each item's rule. A ⌘ shortcut does nothing while its item is greyed.
403	
404	If the item should be on, check these first:
405	
406	| Check | Why it matters |
407	| --- | --- |
408	| The selection | Many commands need a clip selected, or a certain kind of clip. |
409	| A sheet | While a sheet is open, every editor command is off. Close the sheet first. |
410	| A nest | With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, these are off: **New Project from Range…**, **Make Vertical Version…**, **Rename Graphic…**, **Add Marker**, **Next Marker**, **Previous Marker**, **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** and **Text Behind Subject**. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. |
411	| A text field | **Open Nest**, **Close Nest**, **Delete** and **Ripple Delete** are off while you type, because their keys edit the text. |
412	| A key | A command that needs your own key stays in the menu, greyed, and its title ends "(needs your AssemblyAI key)". Rest the pointer on it to see which key and where to set it. Saving the key turns it on at once. See [A feature asks for a key](#a-feature-asks-for-a-key). |
413	
414	## A key does nothing
415	
416	Single-letter keys and the arrow keys belong to the editor window, and they stand down in two cases.
417	
418	- **You're typing in a field.** Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click outside the field, to give the keys back to the editor.
419	- **A sheet is open.** Close it first. In a sheet, <kbd>↩</kbd> presses the main button and <kbd>⎋</kbd> cancels.
420	
421	One more thing can catch you out: with a point selected on a [curve](/color/curves/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point, not the clip.
422	
423	See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/) and [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/).
424	
425	## An edit is refused
426	
427	When the project's rules won't allow an edit, Frame Job beeps, nothing changes, and the rule's own sentence appears at the foot of the inspector after "Refused: ":
428	
429	> Refused: clips 4 and 7 would overlap by 120000 ticks, more than half of the shorter clip (100000 ticks)
430	
431	The sentence stays until the project changes or you click it. It's exact rather than friendly. The clip numbers are Frame Job's own, not positions on the timeline, and a [tick](/reference/glossary/#projects-and-the-timeline) is 1/600,000 of a second. So this one says the overlap would be 0.2 s, and half of the shorter clip is 0.17 s.
432	
433	The rules you'll meet most:
434	
435	| Rule | What it means |
436	| --- | --- |
437	| The overlap rule | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip. |
438	| A locked track | Its clips can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled, and you can't insert onto it or close a gap on it. Unlock it with its [lock button](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
439	| The one-frame minimum | Trims and rolls leave a clip at least one frame long. |
440	| The ends of the file | A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. |
441	
442	Two other results look similar:
443	
444	- **A beep with no message** means the edit would have changed nothing, such as a slip already at the end of the footage. No rule was broken.
445	- **An error alert** means Frame Job couldn't use the request at all, such as a value outside its allowed range.
446	
447	During a drag, positions the rules won't allow are skipped, and the clip waits at the last allowed place. Only the drop counts.
448	
449	See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
450	
451	## A project won't open
452	
453	A project that can't be read fails with a message naming the problem, and Frame Job doesn't rewrite the package.
454	
455	| Message | What to do |
456	| --- | --- |
457	| "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." | The project file inside the package is damaged. Open a backup copy if you have one. |
458	| "project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it" | A newer Frame Job saved it. [Update Frame Job](/getting-started/updates/). |
459	| "too many clips: 5000 (max 4096)", or the same for tracks, markers or media | The file is past one of the [project limits](/reference/limits/#project-size). |
460	
461	Files that have moved don't stop a project opening, and neither does a damaged `cache/` folder. For moved files, see [Clips show a slate](#clips-show-a-slate). Also see [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).
462	
463	## A file won't import
464	
465	Frame Job tells you which file it couldn't add and why.
466	
467	| Message | What it means |
468	| --- | --- |
469	| "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." | This Mac has no AV1 decoder. |
470	| "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." | Only those two VP9 profiles import. |
471	| "*file* is VP8 video, which this Mac cannot decode." | This Mac has no decoder for that codec. Other codecs it can't decode get the same sentence with their own name. |
472	| "Could not read *file*." | The file is damaged, or it isn't a format Frame Job reads. |
473	| "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." | The file holds neither. |
474	| "Timed out reading *file*." | The check took longer than 30 seconds, usually because of a stalled network volume. |
475	| "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." | The message names the line of the file and what's wrong with it. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/). |
476	| "Not enough free space to open *file*…" | A WebM or Matroska file needs room for its copy. The sentence says how much. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/). |
477	
478	A file in a codec this Mac decodes still imports even when some of its data is damaged.
479	
480	If macOS can't open a file, you can repackage or convert it with your own ffmpeg. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
481	
482	If the **File ▸ Add Media…** panel won't let you choose a file, drop it on the Media tab instead. The panel lists only the common types. See [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).
483	
484	An agent's `import_media` reports these reasons too.
485	
486	## Clips show a slate
487	
488	A project always opens, even when files it uses have moved or been deleted. Clips whose file is gone keep their place and show a slate, and their rows in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) wear the **missing** badge.
489	
490	When a project opens with files missing, Frame Job offers the **Missing media** sheet once. Choose **Locate…** for a file, then **Relink**. Frame Job also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files by name, so a shoot moved as one folder is usually found in one go. To relink a file later, use **Relink…** on its row in the Media tab. An agent uses `relink_media`.
491	
492	Two other cases show a slate or leave media missing:
493	
494	- A reversed clip shows a slate until its backwards copy has been rendered. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/).
495	- A [conversion made with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#a-lost-conversion-stays-missing) that's gone from Frame Job's [Rewrapped folder](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#the-rewrapped-folder) stays missing until you relink it. A WebM or MKV copy that's gone is [made again](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#if-a-copy-goes-missing) when the project opens, as long as the original is still there.
496	
497	See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
498	
499	## A clip is silent
500	
501	Check these in order. A muted clip, a muted track and a track silenced by a solo all draw the waveform faded.
502	
503	| Check | What to do |
504	| --- | --- |
505	| The clip's own sound | The clip may be muted in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/), or its [sound turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/). |
506	| The track's **Mute** | A muted track is silent. Mute wins over Solo, so a track that's muted and soloed stays silent. |
507	| **Solo** on another track | While any track is soloed, the others are silent, even if the soloed track has nothing on it. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). |
508	| The clip's rate | Above ×12 a clip has no sound, and the Speed section says "Audio is silent above ×12". On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/). |
509	| Whether its sound has rendered | A ramp's sound, and a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, is silent in the preview until its render finishes. A failed render stays failed until the clip's timing changes or you reopen Frame Job. |
510	| **Detach Audio** | After a detach, the picture clip's own sound is off, and the sound is on its linked clip. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). |
511	
512	If the clip plays but [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) or a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) has gone, check its speed. Both play only at normal speed, so a clip with a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame plays without them.
513	
514	## An export won't start or stops
515	
516	An export that fails says why and leaves no finished file. An agent reads the same reason from `export_status`.
517	
518	While the timeline is empty, **File ▸ Export…** is greyed out. Add a clip first.
519	
520	"Preparing…" is a wait, not a stall. An export waits for what it has to draw and play first, such as speed-ramp audio, [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) masks, and sound measurements.
521	
522	| What you see | What to do |
523	| --- | --- |
524	| "Clip *N*'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…" | An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops. Wait for the clip's Status rows to show its loudness, then export again. |
525	| "Clip *N*'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …" | A failed render keeps failing exports until you change the clip's timing or reopen Frame Job. |
526	| "The export was not started: the graphic…" or "The export was stopped at frame *N* of the graphic…" | Frame Job won't export a graphic that can't draw itself. Fix its [module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) and export again. |
527	| "This Mac cannot export with the “*preset*” preset." | This Mac has no encoder for that format. Choose [another format](/export/formats/). |
528	| "An animated GIF is limited to 600 frames and this range is *N*." | Shorten the range, or lower the export frame rate. An APNG has the same limit. See [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/). |
529	| "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…" | ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) won't take a size of a different shape. Use a size from the popup, or one with the same proportions. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). |
530	
531	A queued AV1 or VP9 job can sit waiting for memory, so it hasn't stalled. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
532	
533	:::caution
534	Quitting during an **Export…** progress sheet doesn't ask first, and it leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.
535	:::
536	
537	See [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/).
538	
539	## A feature asks for a key
540	
541	Anything that sends your words or your audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.
542	
543	| Message | What to do |
544	| --- | --- |
545	| "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." | Paste a key under **Transcription** in [Settings](/reference/settings/). |
546	| "No Anthropic API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant." | Paste a key under **Assistant** in Settings. |
547	| "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | The key failed. Check it, and press **Verify** to test it. |
548	
549	A transcript made in one AssemblyAI region can't be seen from the other, so check **Region** too.
550	
551	An agent can't set a key, so a person has to. See [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/).
552	
553	## Recording won't start
554	
555	A recording needs macOS's permissions, and Frame Job asks for each one only when you press Record.
556	
557	- **Screen Recording** is at **System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording**. Once it's on, relaunch Frame Job, then press Record again. Later presses without it open that pane.
558	- **Microphone**, **Camera** and **Input Monitoring** are asked for only when the recording needs them.
559	- If you started Frame Job from a terminal or another app, macOS applies that app's permissions. The panel's note names the launching process and how to relaunch.
560	- If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, nothing can be recorded until one wakes.
561	
562	An agent's `record_screen` never asks for a permission, so a person has to grant it first. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
563	
564	## An agent can't reach Frame Job
565	
566	Only programs running as you can connect, through the `framejob-mcp` helper inside the app.
567	
568	| What you see | What to do |
569	| --- | --- |
570	| The client can't start the helper after you moved Frame Job | In the **MCP** section of [Settings](/reference/settings/#mcp), press **Copy MCP Command** and register the new path. The path is the one you opened Settings from, and it doesn't follow the app. |
571	| "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job." | The helper isn't in this copy. Use a complete copy of the app. |
572	| "Frame Job did not answer at…" | Frame Job launched but wasn't ready within 60 seconds. Later calls in that client session don't launch another copy, so quit the stray copy and try again. |
573	
574	See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).
575	
576	## Related
577	
578	- [Limits](/reference/limits/)
579	- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
580	- [Menus](/reference/menus/)
581	- [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/)
582	- [Glossary](/reference/glossary/)

content.content:
**Channels** chooses which channels of a stereo file a clip plays. It's the fix for a microphone recorded onto one side of a stereo file, which otherwise plays from one speaker only.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Channels"
  tools="set_audio"
/>

## Choose channels

Open the **Channels** section and pick from **Play**. With several clips selected, the choice goes to all of them.

| **Play** | What you hear |
| --- | --- |
| **Both** | The file as it is. This is the default. |
| **Left Only** | The left channel, from both speakers. |
| **Right Only** | The right channel, from both speakers. |
| **Swap Left and Right** | The two channels exchanged. |

For a microphone on one channel, choose **Left Only** or **Right Only**. The voice then plays from both speakers at its own level. [Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/#mix-to-mono) would also put it in both speakers, but averaging it with the silent channel halves its level.

The header of the section shows the current choice. **Reset** there puts it back to **Both**.

## Good to know

- A mono file has only one channel, so the choice has no effect on it.
- On a nest clip the choice has no effect. Set it on the clips inside.
- The Volume section's **Loudness** readout counts the choice, and so does [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode. Normalize in Peak mode reads the file's waveform and doesn't.
- The choice comes after [voice isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) and any [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/), and before the [EQ](/audio/eq/) and [Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/#mix-to-mono). So on a stereo file with a voice effect, it picks from the sound after the effect.
- With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, the choice is what the action changes to. It switches at the action's end with no glide, and its row says "at end".

## With an agent

`set_audio` sets this with `channels`: `both`, `left`, `right` or `swapped`. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#mono-keep-pitch-pan-and-channels).

## Related

- [Pan and Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/)
- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)
- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/)

    // MARK: - Finder drops

    private func droppedURLs(_ sender: any NSDraggingInfo) -> [URL] {
        let options: [NSPasteboard.ReadingOptionKey: Any] = [.urlReadingFileURLsOnly: true]
        let urls = sender.draggingPasteboard.readObjects(forClasses: [NSURL.self], options: options)
        return (urls as? [URL]) ?? []
    }

    override func draggingEntered(_ sender: any NSDraggingInfo) -> NSDragOperation {
        droppedURLs(sender).isEmpty ? [] : .copy
    }

    override func draggingUpdated(_ sender: any NSDraggingInfo) -> NSDragOperation {
        droppedURLs(sender).isEmpty ? [] : .copy
    }

    override func performDragOperation(_ sender: any NSDraggingInfo) -> Bool {
        let urls = droppedURLs(sender)
        guard !urls.isEmpty else { return false }
        inspector?.onImportFiles?(urls)
        return true
    }
}

Duplicate makes copies of clips without going through the clipboard. Press a key to put them right after the originals, or hold ⌥ and drag them where you want them.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Edit ▸ Duplicate"
  keys={['⌘D', '⌥-drag']}
  where="The Duplicate button in the timeline bar"
  tools={['duplicate', 'move_clip']}
/>

## Duplicate the selection

Select one or more clips and press <kbd>⌘D</kbd>. **Edit ▸ Duplicate** and the timeline bar's **Duplicate** button do the same. With nothing selected, the menu item is greyed out and the button beeps.

The button sits in the [timeline bar](/getting-started/editor-window/#timeline-bar) with the other one-click clip tools, which split, trim, ripple delete and add markers, text and shapes.

Each copy goes on the same track as its original, starting right after the selection's span. A selection of several clips keeps its internal timing: if it runs from 10 s to 14 s, every copy starts 4 s later than its original.

The copies are one undo step, called Duplicate.

## Drag a copy

To place copies somewhere else, hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press on a clip, then drag. The copies follow the pointer and the originals stay where they are.

- If the clip you press is part of the selection, the whole selection is copied. If it isn't, only that clip is.
- The copies snap and change tracks as a [move](/editing/move-clips/) does. Drop past the top or bottom of the stack to make a new track for them.
- A spot the timeline can't take is skipped. The copies stay at the last spot along the drag that worked, and if none did, nothing changes.
- The whole drag is one undo step, called Duplicate Clips.

Hold only <kbd>⌥</kbd>. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on a clip is a [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/), not a copy.

:::caution
An ⌥-drag makes its copies by duplicating first, so it needs the room a <kbd>⌘D</kbd> would need. If Duplicate [wouldn't work](#when-duplicate-wont-work) at that moment, because the next clip is hard up against the selection, the drag moves the originals instead. Undo it, then [copy and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) the clip, which has no such limit.
:::

## Drag a clip

Drag a clip's body left or right to move it in time, and up or down to move it to another track. A clip stops at the start of the timeline.

The drag [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) to nearby edits when snapping is on. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag to turn snapping off for that moment.

## Split at the playhead

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the frame you want to cut on.

2. Select the clips to cut, or select nothing to cut everything under the playhead.

3. Press <kbd>⌘T</kbd>, choose **Clip ▸ Split**, or click the scissors button in the timeline bar.

</Steps>

| What's selected | What gets cut |
| --- | --- |
| One or more clips | Each selected clip the playhead is inside |
| Nothing | Every clip under the playhead on every unlocked track |

It's one undo step, named Split, however many clips it cuts. The command is available whenever the timeline has clips.

The playhead has to be strictly inside a clip. A playhead sitting exactly on a clip's edge is at a cut already, so that clip is left alone. If nothing can be cut, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.

A clip on a locked track is left alone when nothing is selected, but it's still cut if you selected it.

## Footage stays continuous

The second piece carries on playing the footage from where the first stopped, at the same speed, so the split doesn't show when you play it back. If an action is animating the clip, the second piece starts from where that animation had got to at the cut, such 

On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the two pieces meet at exactly the same point in the footage, and the second starts at the rate in force at the cut.

---
title: Make Vertical Version
description: Turn a landscape edit into a tall or square version for a phone, a reel or a square post, in one step over the whole timeline.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Make Vertical Version makes a tall or square version of a landscape edit, for a phone, a reel or a square post. It changes the canvas and reworks the whole timeline in one step, so you don't have to frame each clip yourself.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
  tools="make_vertical_version"
  needs="Nothing. Faces, people and shot changes are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Make a vertical version

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. It's available when the project has a clip, no [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, no other sheet is up and nothing is recording.

2. Pick a [**Shape**](#shape).

3. Choose what to [**Follow**](#follow), and set [**Zoom**](#zoom) and [**Where Empty**](#where-empty) if you want to.

4. Leave [**Make a copy**](#make-a-copy) ticked to keep this project as it is, or untick it to change this project.

5. [Read the summary](#read-the-summary) under the controls. It says what will happen before anything does.

6. Choose **Make** (<kbd>Return</kbd>), or **Cancel** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) to leave everything as it was.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="15j-make-vertical-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Make Vertical Version sheet, with Shape on 9:16 (540 × 960), Follow on Subject, Zoom at 100 %, Where Empty on Show Whole and Make a copy ticked. The summary under them reads: Makes a 540 × 960 version. Keeps 4 clips as placed."
/>

Each clip is treated by what it is: full-frame movies follow their subject, screen recordings follow the pointer, camera layouts are laid out again, and so on. [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/) goes through it clip by clip.

## The controls

### Shape

Each row shows the size it makes, such as **9:16 (1080 × 1920)**. The new canvas keeps the old short side, rounded down to an even number, and the height follows from the shape.

| Shape | From 1920 × 1080 |
| --- | --- |
| **9:16** | 1080 × 1920 |
| **4:5** | 1080 × 1350 |
| **1:1** | 1080 × 1080 |

A shape the canvas already has isn't in the list.

### Follow

What each movie clip keeps in the frame.

...

| Choice | What the frame follows |
| --- | --- |
| **Subject** | A face. Where there's no face, a person. Where there's neither, the region the eye goes to. |
| **Faces** | Faces only. |
| **People** | People only. |
| **Salient Region** | Only the region the eye goes to. |
| **Speaker** | Whoever is talking, for a wide shot with a microphone per person. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/). |
| **Center** | The middle of the picture, for the whole clip. Needs no analysis, so the summary is ready at once. |

These are the choices of [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/), plus **Speaker**. The two commands share one remembered choice, saved when you choose **Make**. It starts on **Subject**. If you last chose **Speaker**, Follow Subject, which doesn't offer it

### Zoom

How tight the frame is, from 100 to 400 %, in whole numbers. 100 % is the smallest scale at which a picture covers the new canvas. Higher values frame closer.

**Zoom** starts at 100 % each time you choose the command and isn't remembered. The one exception is the sheet that [comes back after a Speaker analysis](/framing/follow-speaker/#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis), which keeps what you set. The summary updat

### Where Empty

What a followed clip shows while there's nothing to follow.

| Choice | What the frame shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Show Whole** | The whole picture on a blurred copy of itself. This is the default. |
| **Center** | The middle of the picture. |

It's dimmed while **Follow** is **Center**. It's the same remembered choice as Follow Subject's.

### Make a copy

Ticked, the vertical version opens as a new untitled project and this project doesn't change. The copy is named after this project with the shape, such as "Interview (9:16)", "Interview (4:5)" or "Interview (1:1)". It carries the project's caches and analysis.

Unticked, this project itself becomes the vertical version.

The box is ticked each time you choose the command, and your choice isn't remembered. Only the sheet that comes back after a Speaker analysis keeps what you chose.

## Read the summary

Under the controls, the sheet says what **Make** will do, and it changes as you change a control. It opens with the new size, "Makes a 1080 × 1920 version.", and goes on with whichever of these apply:

| The summary says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Follows 3 clips." | Every clip that's followed, so it includes the clips the next two rows count. |
| "Follows the cursor in 2 clips, their own zooms and pans replaced." | Screen recordings that follow the pointer. |
| "Follows whoever is talking in 1 clip." | Wide shots framed on the speaker. |
| "Re-lays 2 camera layouts for the new canvas." | Camera layout switches made again. |
| "Shows 1 clip whole on a blurred copy." | Clips with nothing to follow at any point. |
| "Keeps 4 clips as placed." | Clips moved and scaled to the new canvas, not framed. |
| "Re-fills 1 background." | Blurred copies and background plates resized to cover the new canvas. |
| "Removes 1 blurred copy the framing replaces." | Old blurred copies that are no longer needed. |
| "Re-sizes 1 graphic to the new canvas." | Graphics exactly the old canvas's size. |
| "Updates 1 graphic module to the current template." | Older copies of a bundled template, in a copy only. |
| "Adds a Backgrounds track for the blurred copy." | A new track at the back for the blurred copies. |
| "Adds 1 more track behind it where clips overlap." | A further track, for copies that overlap in time. |
| "2 actions re-eased at a cut." | A shot change landed inside actions a clip already had, so each was split there and eased again on either side. |
| "2 actions carry a framing move." | A framing move couldn't fit between a clip's own actions, so those actions carry it. |
| "Re-lays 1 caption track for the new canvas." | Word captions paged again for the narrow frame. |

After those come single lines for what needs your attention:

- One line per camera layout switch: "Re-laid: Side by Side → Stacked at 00:00:10:00."
- One line per clip that isn't followed, or is only partly followed, with the reason: "Clip 6 is not followed: its media file is missing, so it is kept as placed." or "Clip 2 is followed, but it is shown whole on a blurred copy where no subject is found."
- One line per caption track that's kept as it was, and one per graphic module left as it is.

If the movies have already been analysed, the summary reads "Reading the analysis…" for a moment, and **Make** is dimmed until it's done.

---
title: "Preview Quality"
description: Draw the preview at half or a quarter of the canvas size so a heavy project plays more smoothly, without changing what you export.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Preview Quality draws the preview smaller and scales it back up to fit, so a heavy project plays more smoothly. It never changes an export.

<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Preview Quality" />

## Full, Half, Quarter

Choose **View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full**, **Half** or **Quarter**. The menu checks the current choice. The preview redraws straight away, paused or playing.

| Choice | Draws the preview at | 1920 × 1080 canvas |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Full** (default) | The canvas size | 1920 × 1080 |
| **Half** | Half the width and height | 960 × 540 |
| **Quarter** | A quarter of the width and height | 480 × 270 |

The choice is remembered between launches, for every project. There's no keyboard shortcut, and no agent tool sets it. The [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) shows the same picture, so it draws at the same quality.

## What it changes

Quality only affects the preview. It never changes an export, a [saved frame](/export/save-frame/) or a frame an agent renders.

A lower choice saves the work of drawing each pixel of the picture. Decoding your footage, drawing shadows and playing the sound cost the same at every choice, so a project held back by those won't speed up as much.

## Good to know

The picture always keeps the canvas's exact shape, so that handles stay in the right place on it. On an awkward canvas size that means the preview can draw a little larger than the fraction, never smaller:

| Canvas | Half | Quarter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 999 × 666 | 501 × 334 | 252 × 168 |
| 1001 × 667 | 1001 × 667 | 1001 × 667 |

A canvas whose sides share no common factor, like 1001 × 667, can't be scaled down evenly, so it draws at full size at every choice.

## Related

- [The preview](/timeline/preview/)
- [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/)
- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)

title: Duck by Speech
description: Lower the other clips only while this clip's speech plays, so the music comes back up in the pauses.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Duck by Speech lowers the other clips only around this clip's stretches of speech, so the music rises again when the voice stops. It's [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) with **Duck by** set to **Speech**.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking ▸ Duck by"
  tools={['set_audio', 'set_media_speech']}
  needs="Nothing. Speech is detected on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Duck only while someone speaks

<Steps>

1. Select the voice clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.

2. In the **Ducking** section, tick **Duck other audio**.

3. Set **Duck by** to **Speech**.

4. Adjust [Pre-roll and Hold](#set-pre-roll-and-hold) if the music moves too early or too late.

</Steps>

Level, Attack and Release work as they do for [ducking by clip length](/audio/ducking/#the-controls), but apply to each stretch of speech rather than to the whole clip.

## How it follows the speech

For each stretch of speech, the attack starts Pre-roll before the first word, the others hold at Level until Hold after the last word, and the release follows.

The pauses decide how often the music moves:

- A breath under 0.2 s between words doesn't count as a pause.
- Stretches whose Pre-roll and Hold meet count as one. At the defaults, that keeps the music down through any pause of 1 s or less.
- Where one stretch's release meets the next one's attack, the others follow whichever is lower, so the level never dips below Level.

Only the speech in the part of the file the clip plays counts. The stretches follow the clip's speed, reverse and speed ramps.

## Set Pre-roll and Hold

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Pre-roll** | How long before each stretch of speech the others start going down. Quick picks: 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 s. | 0.5 s | 0–5 s |
| **Hold** | How long after each stretch of speech the others stay down before the release. Quick picks: 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 s. | 0.5 s | 0–5 s |

title: Ducking
description: Lower the other clips while this one plays, so music drops under a voice-over and comes back up after it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Ducking lowers the other clips while this one plays. The usual use is a voice-over: turn ducking on for the voice, and the music drops under it.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking" tools="set_audio" />

## Duck the music under a voice-over

Set ducking on the clip you want to hear, not on the clip that should get quieter.

<Steps>

1. Select the voice clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.

2. Open the **Ducking** section and tick **Duck other audio**.

3. Set **Level** to how loud the music should be under the voice.

</Steps>

Ticking the box starts from the defaults: down to 20 %, over 0.5 s, and back up over 1 s. Unticking it, or choosing **Reset** in the section's header, turns ducking off and forgets the settings. The header shows the leve

## The controls

---
title: "The volume line"
description: See a clip's level over time on the timeline, drag it, and add points to shape it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The volume line is the thin white line over a clip's waveform. It shows how loud that clip plays over time, and you can drag it to change the level without leaving the timeline.

<AtAGlance
  keys="⌥-click"
  where="On a clip's audio part in the timeline"
  tools={['set_audio', 'add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_action']}
/>

## The line on a clip

Every clip with sound draws the line, except a nest clip. It's the level you hear from that clip, with everything that shapes it folded in:

- the clip's **Volume** and its volume actions
- its fades and crossfades
- ducking from other clips
- the track's volume

The top of the clip's audio part is +30 dB (3200 %) and the bottom is −60 dB or quieter. A clip at 100 % sits about a third of the way down.

A clip you can't hear has its line along the bottom. That's a muted clip, one on a muted track, or one silenced by another track's solo.

A small square in the action colour marks each action end that sets the volume. Those squares are the line's points.

title: "Match Audio"
description: "Give several clips the loudness and speech tone of one of them, so takes from different microphones or rooms sit together, in one undo step."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Match Audio makes selected clips sound like one of them, the reference. It sets each other clip's loudness and speech tone in one undo step, which helps when two takes came from different microphones or rooms.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Match Audio…"
  tools="match_audio"
  needs="Nothing. Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."

## Match clips to a reference

<Steps>

1. Select the clips, including the one that already sounds right. You need at least two clips that could play sound. A nest clip or a clip with no sound doesn't count, and with fewer than two the menu item is greyed out.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Match Audio…**.

3. In **Match to:**, choose the reference.

4. Leave **Loudness** and **EQ** ticked, or untick the one you don't want. **Match** is greyed out with both off.

5. Choose **Match**.

</Steps>

The Measuring Sound sheet stays up while each clip is measured, which takes a moment on a long clip. It counts "Clip 1 of 3…" as it goes. Nothing changes until every clip is measured, and **Cancel** leaves everything as it is.

When it finishes, the change is one undo step called "Match Audio". The results are ordinary settings in the [Volume](/audio/volume/), [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) and [EQ](/audio/eq/) sections, so you can adjust them afterwards.

The sheet opens with both boxes ticked and the first clip chosen every time. It doesn't remember your last choice.

## Choose the reference

**Match to:** lists the clips in timeline order, by start time and then by track, and the first is chosen. Each row reads `name — track — m:ss (clip id)`, for example `Interview — Track 1 — 0:42 (clip 12)`, so you can tell two clips with the same name apart.

The reference itself isn't changed. Frame Job measures it once as it sounds in the timeline: through its own settings, its limiter and its volume, but without its fades, ducking or Mute. Its loudness at that point is the target for the other clips.

## What Loudness sets

**Loudness** runs [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode on each other clip, with the reference's loudness as the target. It sets the clip's volume, measured through the clip's settings as they'll be after the match. When the clip's peaks would pass −

content.content:
A bar sits above the text and stays put while the text scrolls. It holds the two pop-ups, then short notes on what the tab is doing and anything it couldn't read.

**Words from** and **Language** belong to the window. They stay while it's open, whichever tab you look at, and they aren't saved with the project.

### Words from

**Words from** chooses whose words to show: **All tracks**, the default, or one track by name. With one track chosen, the tab shows only the words on it, and reads only the files with a clip on it. If that track goes away, the tab goes back to **All tracks**.

### Language

**Language** chooses the language files are read in on this Mac.

**Automatic** is your Mac's language, shown in brackets as a code such as `en-US`. If you have no speech model for it, Automatic uses another form of the same language, or failing that the first language you have. Below it is every language your Mac has a speech model for. The pop-up is disabled when there are none.

Choosing a language reads the files again in that language. The earlier reading is kept too, so switching back is immediate. A file with an AssemblyAI transcript keeps showing that transcript whichever you choose.

### Read and Stop

----
| Three look boxes | **Slide the pill**, **Fill words as spoken** and **Dim in pauses**. See [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/). | Each as you last left it, off the first time |
| Sample preview | [A sample page](#check-the-sample-preview) in the chosen style. | |
| **Replace:** | [Swaps out earlier caption tracks](#replace-existing-captions) instead of adding another. | Off |

[Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) explains the three AssemblyAI rows.

## Choose what to transcribe

**From:** offers **Selected clips**, **In/out range** and **Whole timeline**. A choice that holds nothing transcribable is greyed.

**In/out range** takes every clip that overlaps the range, whole, so captions can run past the range's edges. Clips that can't be read don't count towards any of the three.

## Choose an engine

**Engine:** chooses where the words are recognised.

| Engine | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **On this Mac** | Recognition runs here and nothing is uploaded. The language's model has to be installed. See [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/). |
| **AssemblyAI** | The audio of each file is uploaded and transcribed in the cloud, on your own key. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/). |

---
title: "Remove Filler Words"
description: "Find the ums and uhs in your speech, see what would go, and cut them all as one edit."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Remove Filler Words finds the ums and uhs in your speech, shows you what it would cut, and cuts them at the words' own timings, all as one undo step. There's nothing to tune.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…"
  tools={['detect_fillers', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript']}
  needs="An AssemblyAI key, unless a file it would read already has a transcript made with filler words."
/>

## Remove the filler words

<Steps>

1. If you only want some clips read, select them. See [Which clips are read](#which-clips-are-read).

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. It's after **Remove Silences…** and has no keyboard shortcut.

3. If the sheet lists files with no filler transcript yet, press **Transcribe** beside each one you want read. This uploads the file's audio to AssemblyAI and costs money, so the sheet shows the estimate first. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/).

4. Check what's shaded on the timeline, and read the count in the sheet, such as "3 cuts · removes 00:00:01:12".

5. Choose **Remove**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was. Closing the sheet also stops a transcription that's still running.

</Steps>

**Remove** is off while the sheet reads "No cuts" and while a transcription is running. One <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> puts everything back, because the whole cut is a single **Remove Filler Words** undo step.

The command is available when the timeline has a clip that plays sound from a media file, forwards, with its sound on, and you've either set an AssemblyAI key or a file it would read already has a transcript made with filler words. With neither, it's greyed and reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs yo

## Which words are fillers

A word counts as a filler when it's on this fixed list, ignoring capitals and any punctuation at its ends:

um · uh · hmm · mhm · uh-huh · ah · huh · hm · m · er · erm

"Uh huh" written as two words matches as two fillers, and "uh-huh" matches as one.

:::caution
The list can't be changed, and the sheet can't keep a single filler. A real "ah" or "er", or the letter "M" said aloud, is treated as a filler too, so check the shading before you choose **Remove**.
:::

## Which clips are read

Remove Filler Words reads the selected clips when the selection includes speech from a media file, and the sheet then says "Only the selected clips are read." Otherwise it reads every clip. The sheet has no menu for this, so make the selection first.

Some clips can't be read:

| Clip | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| It's on a locked track | Its fillers aren't read, because the cut can neither cut nor move it. The sheet counts them: "1 clip is on a locked track, which the cut neither cuts nor moves, so its fillers were not read." |
| It plays in reverse, its sound is switched off, its file is missing, or its file has no audio track | It has no words to read, and it's passed over without a note. |
| It's a [nest](/editing/nests/) | The words inside a nest aren't read from outside it. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and run the command there, where it works on the nest's own timeline. |

When none of those clips has words to read, the sheet says "Nothing in scope plays speech from a media file, so nothing was read."

## What gets cut

Each run of consecutive fillers becomes one cut. A run ends at the next real word, so two fillers with a pause between them and no word go together, pause included. The pauses before and after a run stay. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) takes those out.

The cut is placed to take the whole filler and nothing else:

- It widens outward to the speech grid, the 32 ms steps Frame Job measures speech in, so all of the filler goes. It never reaches into the words on either side.
- Its edges then snap inward to whole frames, as Remove Silences' do. Up to a frame of the filler can remain at each end.

Cuts that touch or overlap join into one, and the count in the sheet is of the joined cuts.

After that it's a normal clean-up cut. It runs across every unlocked track, closes the timeline over each cut, and markers keep their place. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).

---
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Remove Silences finds the dead air in a spoken recording, shows you what it would cut, and takes it all out as one undo step, closing the timeline over each cut. Use it on a screencast, a tutorial or a talking-head take.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Silences…"
  tools={['detect_silence', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
  needs="Nothing. Voice detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Remove the silences

<Steps>

1. To measure only some clips, select them first. The sheet then opens on **Selected clips**.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Remove Silences…**. It's available when the timeline has a clip with its sound on. If there turns out to be nothing to measure, Frame Job beeps instead of opening the sheet.

3. Check what's shaded on the timeline, and read the count in the sheet, for example "23 cuts · removes 00:00:04:12". Both update as you change a control. With nothing to cut the count reads "No cuts" and **Remove** is dimmed.

4. Adjust the [controls](#the-controls) until the cuts look right.

5. Choose **Remove**. Everything shaded is cut and the timeline closes up. <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> puts it all back. Choose **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="14-remove-silences-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Remove Silences sheet, with Judge by set to Voice, a Level if no voice slider at −40 dBFS, Longer than 0.5 seconds, Keep at ends 0.1 seconds, and In set to All audible clips."
/>

The sheet opens on its defaults every time. It doesn't remember your last settings.

## The controls

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Judge by:** | How a moment is tested. See [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/). | Voice, or Level if the voice model can't be used | Voice, Level |
| **Quieter than:** or **Level if no voice:** | The level that counts as quiet. The row reads **Quieter than:** in Level mode and **Level if no voice:** in Voice mode. | −40 dBFS | −80 to −10 dBFS |
| **Longer than:** | The shortest quiet stretch worth cutting. Shorter pauses, such as the gap between two words, stay. | 0.5 s | 0.05 to 10 s |
| **Keep at ends:** | How much of each quiet stretch to keep at each end, so speech doesn't start or stop abruptly. | 0.1 s | 0 to 2 s |
| **In:** | Whether to look at **Selected clips** or **All audible clips**. | Selected clips when the selection has something audible, otherwise All audible clips | |

The level row is a slider in whole decibels, with its value beside it. In Level mode, sound at or below it is quiet. In Voice mode, it judges clips that hold no voice, and a clip the mix turns down to it or lower is quiet whatever it contains.

**Selected clips** is greyed out when nothing selected makes a sound, and a selection of muted clips counts as nothing audible, as does a selected nest. Choose it to stop a music bed under a voice-over from holding the cuts up.

**Longer than:** measures the stretch as you hear it, before **Keep at ends:** takes its share. A stretch no longer than twice **Keep at ends:** isn't cut. Cuts then [round to whole frames](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/#frame-accurate-edges), so up to a fram

The two number fields take up to two decimal places. A number outside the range stays in the field and **Remove** beeps until you fix it. The count and the shading follow the slider as it moves, and a number field when you leave it.

## What the sheet tells you

---

A J-cut brings in the next shot's sound before its picture. An L-cut lets a shot's sound run on under the next shot. Both soften a cut, and in Frame Job both come from trimming the sound half of a [detached clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/).

<AtAGlance
  keys={['W', 'E']}
  where={["Timeline: drag a detached sound clip's edge", 'Timeline: ⌥⇧-drag an edge to roll']}
  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end', 'roll']}
/>

## Make a J-cut

<Steps>

1. Select the later shot and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd> to [detach its audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/#detach-audio).

2. If the shot before it is detached too, drag this sound to a track of its own. See [Keep the sound off its neighbour](#keep-the-sound-off-its-neighbour).

3. Drag the sound clip's start edge to the left.

</Steps>

The sound now begins before its picture. The picture stays where it is.

## Make an L-cut

<Steps>

1. Select the earlier shot and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>.

2. If the next shot's sound is on the track the sound went to, drag this sound to a track of its own.

3. Drag the sound clip's end edge to the right.

---
Each track has its own volume and pan, applied on top of every clip on it. Use them to balance a music bed against a voice-over without touching each clip.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Track ▸ Mix…"
  where={['The sliders switch in the track header', "Mix… in the track's right-click menu"]}
  tools="set_track"
/>

## Open the Track Mix panel

Click the sliders switch, the fifth in the track's header. **Mix…** in the track's right-click menu does the same. **Track ▸ Mix…** opens it for the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track), and has no keyboard shortcut.

A small panel opens beside the header, with the track's name at the top. It holds **Volume**, **Pan**, the track's [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/), and **Reset**.

There's one panel per timeline, so opening it on another track closes the first. Clicking away closes it, and so does anything that takes its track away: removing the track, undoing it away, or going into or out of a nest.

The sliders switch is lit while the track's volume or pan is off its default, or a compressor or limiter is on.

## Set a track's volume

| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Volume** | The track's level, as a slider and a field in dB. Beside them, a readout shows the level as a percentage, or "Off". | Off (at −60) to +12 dB | 0 dB |
---
Mute silences one track. Solo silences every other track, so you can hear one part of the mix by itself. Neither touches the picture.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Track ▸ Mute Audio', 'Track ▸ Solo']}
  where={['The speaker and headphones switches in the track header', "The track's right-click menu"]}
  tools="set_track"
/>

## Mute a track

Click the speaker switch in the track's header. Every clip on the track goes silent, and the picture is unaffected. Click it again to bring the sound back.

**Mute Audio** in the track's right-click menu does the same for the track you clicked. **Track ▸ Mute Audio** acts on the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track): the track of the first selected clip, or the front track when n

To silence one clip and not its whole track, use its own [**Mute**](/audio/volume/#mute-a-clip).

## Solo a track

Click the headphones switch in the track's header, or choose **Solo** in the track's right-click menu or the **Track** menu. The tracks beside it go silent: the other timeline tracks or, inside a nest, that nest's other tracks.

You can solo several tracks. All the soloed tracks play, and the rest are silenced.

**Solo** shows a checkmark in the **Track** menu while it's on. Neither **Solo** nor **Mute Audio** has a keyboard shortcut. Each click is one undo step, named "Mute Track" or "Solo Track".

## How mute and solo combine

- **Mute always wins.** A track that's both muted and soloed stays silent.
---
**Hide Video** takes a track's picture out of your video and leaves its clips where they are. **Lock Track** protects a track's clips while you edit everything around them.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Track ▸ Hide Video', 'Track ▸ Lock Track']}
  where={['The eye and padlock switches in a track header', 'Right-click a track header or an empty stretch of its lane']}
  tools={['set_track']}
/>

## Hide Video

Click the eye in the track's header. It becomes a struck-through eye and the track's clips draw dimmed on the timeline. Click it again to bring the picture back.

**Hide Video** in the [track context menu](/timeline/manage-tracks/#the-track-context-menu) does the same for the track you clicked, and **Track ▸ Hide Video** for the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track).
