content.content:
Generate Captions can only read clips that play recorded sound. Before a run starts, Frame Job works out which clips those are. Use this page when a clip gets left out, or when a long project stops a run.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…" tools="transcribe" />

## Which clips can be transcribed

A clip can be transcribed when all of these are true:

- It plays a movie or sound file that has an audio track.
- It plays forwards.
- Its audio is on.
- Its file is present.

**File ▸ Generate Captions…** is greyed out when no clip on the open timeline plays sound from a media file, forwards, with its audio on.

## Why a clip is skipped

A clip that can't be read isn't part of the run. In the [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) sheet it doesn't count towards the summary line, so if the sheet says 2 clips and you expected 3, the third is here. The sheet doesn't list these clips one by one. If it leav

An agent that names the clips it wants gets the reason back for each one, in these words:

| Reason | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| its source is not a media file, so it has no speech | It's a text, shape, still, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. | For a nest, [open it](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and caption inside it. |
| it plays in reverse, so its speech cannot be transcribed | The words would come out backwards. | Only a clip playing forwards can be read. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/). |
| its media has no audio track | The file has no sound. | Nothing to transcribe here. |
| its audio is switched off | For example, the picture half of a clip after [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). | After Detach Audio, the audio-only clip below it holds the sound and is read instead. **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** joins the two again. |
| its media file is missing | Frame Job can't find the file. | [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/). |
| its speed ramps, and no speed map was read for it | Frame Job couldn't work out where the ramp puts the words, so it won't guess. | Remove the [ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) if you need this clip captioned. |
| its speed or length is degenerate | The clip has no usable speed or no length. | Add the clip to the timeline again. |

A clip that's read but holds no words shows up afterwards, in the [run report](/captions/generate-captions/#the-run-report), as "no speech was recognised in it".

## Retimed clips land correctly

On a sped-up, slowed or speed-ramped clip, each word lands where it's heard on the timeline, not where it sits in the file. Transcribing a ramped clip places each word where the ramp plays it.

Captions keep following afterwards. Change the speed later and they move with the speech. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).

## The 10-hour and 4,096-clip limits

**AssemblyAI takes at most 10 hours per file.** What counts is the length of the whole file, not the part your clip uses, because the whole file is what's sent. Frame Job won't extract or send a longer file, and its clips are listed in the [run report](/captions/generate-captions

---
Remove Silences cuts a stretch only when it's quiet as you hear it, in the mix, and only where every clip it's measuring is quiet at once. The **In:** menu sets which clips those are. **Judge by:** in the sheet picks how each moment is tested.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Silences…"
  where="Judge by: in the Remove Silences sheet"
  tools="detect_silence"
  needs="Nothing. Voice detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Judge by Voice or Level

| **Judge by:** | A moment is quiet when |
| --- | --- |
| **Voice** | Nobody is talking. |
| **Level** | The sound in the mix is at or below the threshold. |

The sheet opens on **Voice** every time, unless [the voice model can't be used](#when-the-voice-model-cant-be-used).

Voice listens for speech, not for loudness. A low recording level doesn't make speech quiet, and in a clip that holds a voice, a loud sound that isn't speech, such as a hum, still counts as quiet. If a recording has sounds you want to keep, such as the audio of a demo, choose **L

## Voice mode

A voice-activity model that comes with Frame Job (Silero VAD) scores every 32 ms of a file for how likely it is to be speech. A moment counts as speech when its score reaches the voice confidence, a value from 0 to 1 that the sheet always holds at 0.5.

You don't start the analysis. It runs by itself after you import a file or open a project, listens to each file once and keeps the answer with the project. It runs on your Mac, and nothing is uploaded.

In Voice mode the threshold row reads **Level if no voice:**, and it does two jobs:

- It's the level for [clips with no voice in them](#clips-with-no-voice-are-judged-by-level).
- A clip the mix turns down to that level or lower is quiet whatever it holds. At the default −40 dBFS, that's a clip turned down by 40 dB or more.

The same voice analysis also serves [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/), [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/), [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/), [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/), [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) and the [transcr

    override var acceptsFirstResponder: Bool { true }

    /// The URLs on the pasteboard this app claims — the `.framejob` package
    /// and every movie/audio/image type the Info.plist lists as an Alternate
    /// handler, which is exactly `ProjectDocument.readableTypes`.
    private func readableURLs(from sender: any NSDraggingInfo) -> [URL] {
        let options: [NSPasteboard.ReadingOptionKey: Any] = [.urlReadingFileURLsOnly: true]
        guard let urls = sender.draggingPasteboard.readObjects(
            forClasses: [NSURL.self], options: options) as? [URL]
        else { return [] }
        let readable = ProjectDocument.readableTypes.compactMap(UTType.init)
        return urls.filter { url in
            guard let type = (try? url.resourceValues(forKeys: [.contentTypeKey]))?.contentType
                ?? UTType(filenameExtension: url.pathExtension)
            else { return false }
            return readable.contains { type.conforms(to: $0) }
        }
    }

    override func draggingEntered(_ sender: any NSDraggingInfo) -> NSDragOperation {
        readableURLs(from: sender).isEmpty ? [] : .copy
    }

    override func performDragOperation(_ sender: any NSDraggingInfo) -> Bool {
        let urls = readableURLs(from: sender)
        for url in urls {
            NSDocumentController.shared.openDocument(
                withContentsOf: url, display: true
            ) { _, _, error in
                if let error = error, (error as? CocoaError)?.code != .userCancelled {
                    NSApp.presentError(error)
                }
            }
        }
        return !urls.isEmpty
    }
}

| [Trim and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone) | On the picture, the edit carries to the sound when their edges line up. On the sound, it moves the sound alone. |
| [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) | Slips both, as far as the one with less room allows. |
| Delete | Deleting the picture deletes its sound too. See [Remove a clip's sound](#remove-a-clips-sound). |
| [Speed](/speed/change-speed/) and [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) | Frame Job won't do these on a linked clip. See [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed). |

A ripple edit that would push a sound starting before its picture past the start of the timeline doesn't happen at all. The reason at the foot of the inspector says the sound "would start before 0".

Locks win over links. A partner on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#lock-track) isn't moved, split, trimmed, slipped, duplicated, nested or deleted with its clip. **Copy** is the exception: a selected picture brings its soun

## Remove a clip's sound

To drop a clip's sound for good, detach it, select the sound half and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. The picture stays, silent, and its link is gone.

Undo brings the sound back. Once the sound clip is gone, no control in the app turns the picture's own audio back on.

## Attach audio

Select either half of a pair and press <kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Attach Audio**. The **Attach Audio** button in the Mix section does the same, but it's only there with the sound half selected, because the picture half has no Sound

The picture's audio comes back on with the sound clip's audio settings, and the sound clip is removed. Its track stays, empty if nothing else is on it. With several pairs selected, each one merges, as one undo step named "Attach Audio".

**Clip ▸ Attach Audio** is greyed out until the selection holds a linked clip. The button stays live, and beeps if the selection holds none.

### When Attach Audio won't work

The two halves have to match, because they're becoming one clip. They need the same start, length, in point and speed, and the same actions at the same times with the same curves. Otherwise the reason at the foot of the inspector says "clip

## Actions and speed

The new sound clip gets a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working. An action that only changes the picture does nothing on the sound clip. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/#detach-audio).

A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) keeps it: the sound clip's copy of the Speed actions gives it the same ramp, so the two stay in step.

Frame Job won't change the speed or direction of either half while they're linked, because the two would have to be re-timed identically. That covers Speed, Reverse, rate stretch, [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/), and adding, moving, ch

Attaching keeps the sound's work. The picture takes the sound clip's audio settings, and each of its actions takes the audio values of the sound clip's action at the same place.

## With an agent

[`detach_audio`](/mcp/tools-audio/#detach_audio) and [`attach_audio`](/mcp/tools-audio/#attach_audio) do what the **Clip** menu does, for the one clip you name in `clip`. For `attach_audio`, either half will do.

`set_enabled` turns a clip's picture or sound on or off directly, which no control in the app does. After a detached sound has been deleted, it's the way to switch the picture's own audio back on. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools

## Paste a clip's attributes

<Steps>

1. Select the clip that has the settings you want and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.

2. Select the clips that should take them.

3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.

</Steps>

The item is available when Frame Job clips are on the clipboard and something is selected. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps. The paste is one undo step, called Paste Attributes.

If you copied several clips, only one of them counts: the one that starts earliest. At the same start it's the one on the front-most track.

## What travels

Settings travel in four groups, and a group is only copied when both clips have it. A movie's settings pasted onto a text clip bring its picture settings and leave the text styling alone, and its sound settings go nowhere.

Each group replaces the target's whole group, so it isn't a merge. A shadow on the target disappears if the copied clip had none.

| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Video** | Everything about the picture: position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, corner radius, blend mode, shadow, reflection, filters, spotlight, obscure regions, chroma key, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, Hide While Silent,
| **Audio** | Everything about the sound: volume, Mute, fades and their shapes, pan, Mix to mono, channels, Keep pitch, ducking, noise reduction, voice isolation, EQ, hum removal, gate, de-esser, leveller, compressor, limiter and voice effe
| **Text** | Font, size, colours, alignment, spacing, case, outline, backdrop, text box width, reveal animation and word caption style | Its own words and their timings |
| **Shape** | Fill, stroke, gradient, corner radius and arrowheads | Its kind, its size and the end points of a line |

:::caution
The Video group includes position and scale. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits.
:::

## When a file goes missing

A project always opens, even with files gone. For each missing file:

- Its clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate, with no sound.
- Its row on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) wears a coral **missing** badge.
- An export still runs, and writes the slate and silence for those clips.

Frame Job remembers a file by more than its path, so one you've moved or renamed is often still found and never shows as missing.

[`make_vertical_version`](/mcp/tools-framing/#make_vertical_version) makes the same version from a named shape. It differs from the sheet in a few ways:

- It can save the copy straight to a place you choose, and the assistant asks first when it does.
- It can leave caption tracks as placed, where the sheet always pages them again.
- It waits up to 60 s for an analysis. Past that nothing is made, and calling it again carries on.
- It takes **Zoom** as 1 to 4 rather than a percentage.

def main() -> None:
    failed = []
    touched = set()
    for rel, old, new in EDITS:
        path = ROOT / rel
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        count = text.count(old)
        if new in text and count <= 1 and old not in new:
            print("already", rel)
            continue
        if count != 1:
            failed.append((rel, count, old[:70]))
            continue
        path.write_text(text.replace(old, new), encoding="utf-8")
        touched.add(rel)
    for item in failed:
        print("FAILED", item)
    print(len(touched), "files touched")
    print(" ".join("docs/site/src/content/docs/" + t for t in sorted(touched)))


main()

A recorder that runs on through several camera files can't be held still from the menu. An agent can do it by naming the recorder as the anchor. See [`sync_audio`](/mcp/tools-audio/#sync_audio).

## Which clips it takes

**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** is available when at least two selected clips can play sound and aren't [nests](/editing/nests/).

Anything else in the selection is left out without a message: a nest, a still, a title, a file with no audio track, a clip with its audio switched off. To line up clips inside a nest, open it with <kb

## The anchor

Frame Job picks the anchor this way:

1. Among the selected clips that have a picture, the one that starts earliest. If none has a picture, all of them are considered.
2. If two start at the same time, the one on the rearmost track.

unanswerable: A recorder's poly WAV with more than two channels: the code didn't settle how it plays or what Channels does to channels 3 and up, so the pages only keep their existing metering notes. A podcaster with a multitrack recorder still has no answer.

app_defects.title: Generate Captions reads muted clips, so a multicam show gets doubled words
app_defects.evidence: TranscribeSheetController.clips(in:) takes every clip and Transcriber.jobs checks only clip.enabled.audio, so Mute and a track mute change nothing. The Transcript tab drops inaudible clips (SilenceDetector.isAudible in TimelineTranscript.swift) and its own note tells you to mute one to read it once. So a muted camera is left out of the transcript but still captioned. Found by reading the code, not by running it.

app_defects.title: Synchronize Audio's menu can't keep a recorder still against a camera
app_defects.evidence: AudioSync.chooseAnchor always prefers a clip with a picture, and only sync_audio's anchor argument overrides it. A recorder running through two camera files moves to whichever file is selected with it, so a camera that stopped and restarted can't be lined up to one long recorder from the menu. This is a design limit, documented in audio/synchronize-audio.

The Transcript tab drops inaudible clips (SilenceDetector.isAudible in TimelineTranscript.swift) and its own note tells you to mute one to read it once. So a muted camera is left out of the transcript but still captioned. Found by reading the code, not by running it.

app_defects.title: Synchronize Audio's menu can't keep a recorder still against a camera
app_defects.evidence: AudioSync.chooseAnchor always prefers a clip with a picture, and only sync_audio's anchor argument overrides it. A recorder running through two camera files moves to whichever file is selected with it, so a camera that stopped and restarted can't be lined up to one long recorder from the menu. This is a design limit, documented in audio/synchronize-audio.

app_defects.title: A folder dropped on the Media tab is treated as one file
app_defects.evidence: MediaPane.performDragOperation passes the folder URL to ProjectDocument.importMedia, and the import path never lists a folder's contents. By reading the code it should fall to the unreadable-file path (AVFoundation probe, then the 'Could not read' alert), not an explanation. The alert itself was not seen in a running app.
